project.name: PracticeTakes
project.description: Practice Takes is an early cross-platform desktop music-practice application for Windows, Linux, and macOS, focused on live microphone analysis (tuner and spectrogram) with a dockable/floating workspace system, and intended to grow into a more complete digital audio workstation.

nodes.name: MainComponent.h
nodes.summary: Declares MainComponent, the application shell that owns the audio input service, theme, workspace layout/tool state, tool windows, settings and feedback windows; its ~80 member functions are implemented across a dozen partner translation units.
nodes.languageNotes: A JUCE 'god component' declared once in a header and split across many .cpp files, each implementing one behavioural slice (lifecycle, appearance, audio, drag, presentation, snapshot, settings, feedback).

nodes.name: WorkspaceStartupSequence.h
nodes.summary: Header-only helper that fixes the startup ordering contract: restore the workspace, then show the window, then defer service initialisation.
nodes.languageNotes: A template static function taking three forwarding-reference callables, so the sequence can be unit tested with plain lambdas and no JUCE dependency.

nodes.name: MainComponentAppearance.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements MainComponent theming: maps the active theme's palette onto every JUCE LookAndFeel colour id and propagates the appearance to top buttons, open tool windows and the settings window.

nodes.name: MainComponentAudioState.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the shell's microphone state surface: reacts to AudioInputService change broadcasts, recolours the microphone button, and shows or dismisses the microphone warning banner.

nodes.name: MainComponent
nodes.summary: The application shell component: owns the audio input service, application properties, theme, tool state, workspace layout tree and every child window, and acts as both drag-and-drop container and target.

nodes.name: WorkspaceStartupSequence
nodes.summary: Static helper whose run() enforces the startup ordering: restore workspace, show window, then defer service initialisation.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Invokes the three startup callables in the guaranteed order: restore the workspace, show the window, then defer service initialisation.

nodes.name: setTheme
nodes.summary: Stores the newly selected theme and re-applies the whole appearance if it actually changed.

nodes.name: applyAppearance
nodes.summary: Re-applies the current palette to the look and feel, top buttons and open windows, then broadcasts a look-and-feel change and repaints.

nodes.name: configureLookAndFeelColours
nodes.summary: Maps the active application palette onto roughly fifty JUCE LookAndFeel colour ids covering windows, buttons, text editors, sliders, combo boxes and popup menus.

nodes.name: applyAppearanceToTopButtons
nodes.summary: Recolours the title-bar buttons for the active palette and refreshes the microphone button state.

nodes.name: applyAppearanceToOpenWindows
nodes.summary: Propagates the current theme and palette to the microphone warning, every open tool, the settings window and the feedback window.

nodes.name: hasUsableMicrophone
nodes.summary: Returns whether the audio input service currently reports a usable microphone input.

nodes.name: changeListenerCallback
nodes.summary: ChangeListener hook: when the audio input service broadcasts, refreshes the microphone button and warning banner.

nodes.name: updateMicrophoneStateControl
nodes.summary: Derives the microphone button's label, tooltip and colours from the current input state (missing, muted, live) using the active palette.

nodes.name: updateMicrophoneWarning
nodes.summary: Shows or hides the microphone warning banner based on usable input and whether the user has already dismissed it.

nodes.name: dismissMicrophoneWarning
nodes.summary: Marks the microphone warning as dismissed for this session and hides the banner.

nodes.name: FeedbackWindow.h
nodes.summary: Defines MainComponent::FeedbackWindow, a resizable JUCE DocumentWindow that hosts FeedbackComponent and reports closure back to the shell.

nodes.name: MainComponentFeedback.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the Help menu, feedback window presentation, and the usage-count driven feedback invitation flow backed by FeedbackInvitationPolicy and persisted application properties.

nodes.name: MainTitleBar.h
nodes.summary: Defines MainTitleBar, the custom non-native title bar hosting the File/Settings/Tools/Help/microphone buttons, window drag handling, and a hamburger menu that collapses those buttons on narrow windows.

nodes.name: MicrophoneWarning.h
nodes.summary: Defines MainComponent::MicrophoneWarning, the themed banner shown when no usable microphone input is available, offering 'Open settings' and 'Dismiss' actions.

nodes.name: SettingsWindow.h
nodes.summary: Defines MainComponent::SettingsWindow and its nested Content/CategoryPanel hierarchy (Appearance, Audio, Practice, Reset), wiring every settings control back to the shell through handler callbacks.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a nested class hierarchy with a shared CategoryPanel base so each settings category owns its own controls and layout.

nodes.name: FeedbackWindow
nodes.summary: DocumentWindow that owns a FeedbackComponent, forwards a context tag into it, and invokes the shell's close handler asynchronously when closed.

nodes.name: MainTitleBar
nodes.summary: Custom title bar component: draws the window title, hosts the menu and window-control buttons, drags the window, and collapses to a hamburger menu when the bar is too narrow.

nodes.name: MicrophoneWarning
nodes.summary: Themed overlay banner warning that no usable microphone is available, with 'Open settings' and 'Dismiss' buttons wired to shell callbacks.

nodes.name: SettingsWindow
nodes.summary: DocumentWindow hosting the settings Content panel; forwards every settings action to shell-provided handlers and re-themes itself on appearance changes.

nodes.name: Content
nodes.summary: Scrollable body of the settings window that instantiates and lays out the Appearance, Audio, Practice and Reset category panels.

nodes.name: CategoryPanel
nodes.summary: Shared base for settings category panels, providing the heading and description label configuration used by every category.

nodes.name: AppearancePanel
nodes.summary: Settings category panel for theme and appearance selection.

nodes.name: AudioPanel
nodes.summary: Settings category panel for microphone mute, input gain and live input level, listening to AudioInputService change broadcasts to keep its controls current.

nodes.name: PracticePanel
nodes.summary: Settings category panel for practice preferences and tuner presets.

nodes.name: ResetPanel
nodes.summary: Settings category panel exposing the reset actions: current tool, audio, layout and everything.

nodes.name: FeedbackWindow
nodes.summary: Constructs the feedback window, owns a FeedbackComponent seeded with the properties file and initial context, and sets resize limits before showing.

nodes.name: setContextTag
nodes.summary: Forwards a context tag (the tool or workflow the user was in) to the hosted FeedbackComponent.

nodes.name: closeButtonPressed
nodes.summary: Hides the window and invokes the shell's close handler asynchronously so the window can safely destroy itself.

nodes.name: showHelpMenu
nodes.summary: Builds and shows the Help popup menu with 'Send feedback' and a toggle that disables future feedback invitations.

nodes.name: showFeedback
nodes.summary: Opens the feedback window (or brings it to front) with the given context tag, creating it against the user settings properties file.

nodes.name: closeFeedback
nodes.summary: Destroys the feedback window.

nodes.name: recordSuccessfulToolUse
nodes.summary: Increments the persisted successful-tool-use counter and then re-evaluates whether a feedback invitation should be offered.

nodes.name: maybeOfferFeedbackInvitation
nodes.summary: Reads the persisted invitation state, asks FeedbackInvitationPolicy whether to invite, and if so shows a yes/no/cancel prompt that can open feedback or permanently opt out.

nodes.name: setFeedbackInvitationsDisabled
nodes.summary: Persists the feedback-invitation opt-out flag and keeps the in-memory copy in sync.

nodes.name: feedbackInvitationsDisabled
nodes.summary: Returns whether the user has opted out of feedback invitations.

nodes.name: MainTitleBar
nodes.summary: Builds the title bar: adopts the shell's menu buttons, creates the hamburger, minimise, fullscreen and close buttons, and stores the supplied window-control handlers.

nodes.name: setFullscreen
nodes.summary: Switches the fullscreen button's glyph and tooltip between enter and exit states.

nodes.name: paint
nodes.summary: Draws the title-bar background, the window title text and the separator line beneath the bar.

nodes.name: resized
nodes.summary: Lays out the window controls on the right and the menu buttons on the left, collapsing the menu buttons into the hamburger button when the bar is too narrow.

nodes.name: mouseDown
nodes.summary: Begins dragging the parent DocumentWindow when the bar itself is pressed.

nodes.name: mouseDrag
nodes.summary: Drags the parent window with the pointer, unless the window is fullscreen or in kiosk mode.

nodes.name: mouseDoubleClick
nodes.summary: Toggles fullscreen when the title bar is double-clicked.

nodes.name: showCollapsedMenu
nodes.summary: Shows the hamburger popup that mirrors the collapsed File/Settings/Tools/Help and microphone actions, triggering the corresponding hidden button on selection.

nodes.name: MicrophoneWarning
nodes.summary: Builds the warning banner's title, message and the 'Open settings' and 'Dismiss' buttons, binding them to the supplied handlers.

nodes.name: setTheme
nodes.summary: Stores the theme and recolours the banner's buttons from the matching palette.

nodes.name: paint
nodes.summary: Draws the banner's drop shadow, rounded card, accent stripe, warning dot and glyph using the active palette.

nodes.name: resized
nodes.summary: Lays out the warning glyph column, the title and message labels, and the action buttons.

nodes.name: SettingsWindow
nodes.summary: Constructs the settings window and its Content panel, passing through the audio service, initial theme and the thirteen shell handlers for appearance, presets, save/import/export, feedback, resets and close.

nodes.name: applyAppearance
nodes.summary: Applies a new palette, background colour and theme to the settings window and its content.

nodes.name: DockedToolPanel.h
nodes.summary: Defines MainComponent::DockedToolPanel, the titled container for a docked tool that adds a drag handle, options button and drag-threshold logic for tearing the tool out into a floating window.

nodes.name: ToolDragHandle.h
nodes.summary: Defines ToolDragHandle, a small painted grip component that starts a workspace tool drag once the pointer moves past a threshold.

nodes.name: ToolOptionsButton.h
nodes.summary: Defines ToolOptionsButton, the per-tool overflow button whose popup menu offers dock/float, 'Send feedback' and close actions.

nodes.name: ToolWindow.h
nodes.summary: Defines MainComponent::ToolWindow, the floating JUCE DocumentWindow wrapper for a tool, with focus tracking, appearance application and drag-to-dock support.

nodes.name: MainComponentWorkspaceDrag.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the shell's drag-and-drop target behaviour: computing drop-zone geometry and labels, painting the drop overlay, resolving a pointer position to a pane plus zone, and committing the resulting dock/float/relocate operation.

nodes.name: DockedToolPanel
nodes.summary: Container for a docked tool: renders a titled frame, hosts a drag handle and options button, and starts a tear-out drag once the pointer passes a movement threshold.

nodes.name: ToolDragHandle
nodes.summary: Painted grip component that fires the workspace drag handler once the pointer moves beyond the drag threshold.

nodes.name: ToolOptionsButton
nodes.summary: Text button that opens a per-tool popup menu offering dock/float, send-feedback and close actions.

nodes.name: ToolWindow
nodes.summary: Floating DocumentWindow wrapper for a tool component, handling close, focus changes, appearance application and drag-to-dock.

nodes.name: DockedToolPanel
nodes.summary: Builds the docked panel: stores the tool content, creates the drag handle and options button, and wires the float, feedback, close and focus handlers.

nodes.name: ~DockedToolPanel
nodes.summary: Releases the borrowed tool content back to the shell before the panel is destroyed.

nodes.name: releaseContent
nodes.summary: Detaches the hosted tool component so it can be re-parented into a floating window without being destroyed.

nodes.name: paint
nodes.summary: Draws the docked panel's frame and title strip.

nodes.name: resized
nodes.summary: Lays out the title strip, drag handle, options button and the tool content area.

nodes.name: mouseDown
nodes.summary: Records the press origin and starts a tear-out drag if the press already qualifies.

nodes.name: mouseDrag
nodes.summary: Starts the workspace drag once the pointer has moved past the drag threshold from the press origin.

nodes.name: canStartDrag
nodes.summary: Decides whether a mouse event should begin a tear-out drag, excluding presses that land on the panel's own controls.

nodes.name: ToolDragHandle
nodes.summary: Stores the drag handler and sets the grip's mouse cursor.

nodes.name: paint
nodes.summary: Draws the grip dots that signal the handle is draggable.

nodes.name: mouseDrag
nodes.summary: Fires the drag handler once the pointer moves past the threshold from the press origin.

nodes.name: ToolOptionsButton
nodes.summary: Stores the presentation, feedback and close handlers and wires the button click to open its options menu.

nodes.name: showOptions
nodes.summary: Shows the tool options popup offering dock/float toggling, 'Send feedback' and close, dispatching the chosen action to the stored handlers.

nodes.name: ToolWindow
nodes.summary: Constructs the floating tool window around a borrowed tool component, adding the drag handle and options button and applying the preferred size and resize limits.

nodes.name: ~ToolWindow
nodes.summary: Releases the borrowed tool content back to the shell before destroying the window.

nodes.name: activeWindowStatusChanged
nodes.summary: Reports focus gain back to the shell so the newly active tool becomes the current tool.

nodes.name: releaseContent
nodes.summary: Detaches the hosted tool component so it can be re-docked without being destroyed.

nodes.name: applyAppearance
nodes.summary: Applies a palette and background colour to the tool window chrome.

nodes.name: resized
nodes.summary: Lays out the window's drag handle and options button over the content area.

nodes.name: mouseDown
nodes.summary: Records the press origin and starts a drag-to-dock gesture if the press qualifies.

nodes.name: mouseDrag
nodes.summary: Starts the drag-to-dock gesture once the pointer moves past the drag threshold.

nodes.name: canStartDrag
nodes.summary: Decides whether a mouse event should begin a drag-to-dock gesture, excluding presses on the window's own controls.

nodes.name: dropZoneBounds
nodes.summary: Computes the highlight rectangle for a drop zone (centre, the four edges, or the floating strip) inside the given workspace bounds.

nodes.name: dropZoneLabel
nodes.summary: Maps a drop zone to the human-readable label shown in the drag overlay.

nodes.name: paintDropZone
nodes.summary: Paints one drop-zone rectangle with its label, using a stronger fill and outline when the zone is the active target.

nodes.name: beginToolDrag
nodes.summary: Starts a JUCE drag-and-drop operation carrying the tool identity, optionally with a drag image.

nodes.name: draggedTool
nodes.summary: Decodes the tool type out of a drag-source description, returning nullopt when the payload is not one of ours.

nodes.name: dockedToolAt
nodes.summary: Finds which docked tool pane, if any, contains the given shell-relative position.

nodes.name: resolveDropTarget
nodes.summary: Turns a pointer position into a drop target: the pane under the cursor plus the drop zone within it, or the floating zone outside the workspace.

nodes.name: isInterestedInDragSource
nodes.summary: Accepts a drag only when its description decodes to one of the workspace tools.

nodes.name: itemDragEnter
nodes.summary: Resolves and stores the active drop target when a drag enters the shell, then repaints the overlay.

nodes.name: itemDragMove
nodes.summary: Re-resolves the drop target as the pointer moves and repaints only when the target actually changed.

nodes.name: itemDropped
nodes.summary: Commits the drop: floats the tool, or docks it and inserts it into the layout tree at the resolved pane and zone, then rebuilds the workspace and focuses the tool.

nodes.name: paintOverChildren
nodes.summary: Draws the drag overlay on top of the workspace: every candidate drop zone plus the highlighted active target.

nodes.name: MainComponentWorkspacePresentation.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements tool presentation for the shell: opening, docking, floating, focusing and closing tools, constructing the matching DockedToolPanel or ToolWindow, and creating and theming the underlying analysis components.

nodes.name: MainComponentWorkspaceSnapshot.cpp
nodes.summary: Captures and restores workspace snapshots: encodes tuner settings into a bounded tool-settings payload, records tool presentations and bounds, and rebuilds the whole workspace from a stored snapshot.

nodes.name: main.cpp
nodes.summary: Application entry point: defines PracticeTakesApplication and its MainWindow, which owns MainComponent, drives the fullscreen/kiosk handling per platform, and runs the restore-show-defer startup sequence.
nodes.languageNotes: START_JUCE_APPLICATION-style bootstrap; fullscreen is implemented separately for Windows, macOS and Linux because JUCE kiosk mode behaves differently on each.

nodes.name: PracticeTakesApplication
nodes.summary: JUCEApplication subclass supplying the application name/version, creating the MainWindow on initialise and releasing it on shutdown.

nodes.name: MainWindow
nodes.summary: Top-level DocumentWindow that owns MainComponent, installs the custom title bar, runs the startup sequence, and implements per-platform fullscreen and kiosk toggling.

nodes.name: openTool
nodes.summary: Entry point for opening a tool: focuses it if already open in the requested presentation, otherwise presents it.

nodes.name: presentTool
nodes.summary: Docks, floats or closes a tool: creates the component if needed, updates the tool state and layout tree, then builds the presentation, rebuilds the container and applies the appearance.

nodes.name: constructToolPresentation
nodes.summary: Builds the concrete host for a tool - a DockedToolPanel or a ToolWindow - and wires its drag, dock/float, feedback, close and focus callbacks back to the shell.

nodes.name: focusTool
nodes.summary: Makes a tool the current one, bringing its window or docked pane to the front and recording the focus change.

nodes.name: recordToolFocus
nodes.summary: Stores the newly focused tool and re-captures the active workspace snapshot.

nodes.name: closeTool
nodes.summary: Closes a tool: saves its settings, detaches the presentation, removes it from the layout tree and tool state, rebuilds the container, re-captures the snapshot and records a successful tool use.

nodes.name: createToolComponent
nodes.summary: Factory that instantiates the tuner, spectrogram or harmonic analyzer component and applies the saved settings and current theme to it.

nodes.name: toolName
nodes.summary: Returns the display name for a tool type.

nodes.name: preferredToolWindowSize
nodes.summary: Returns the default floating window size for each tool type.

nodes.name: toolIsOpen
nodes.summary: Reports whether a tool currently has any presentation open.

nodes.name: detachToolPresentation
nodes.summary: Tears down a tool's current host, first releasing the shared tool component so it survives to be re-hosted, and remembers the window bounds.

nodes.name: applyAppearanceToTool
nodes.summary: Applies the current palette and theme to a tool's host window or docked panel and to the tool component itself.

nodes.name: workspaceBounds
nodes.summary: Converts a JUCE rectangle into the serialisable WorkspaceBounds value used by snapshots.

nodes.name: tunerPayload
nodes.summary: Encodes the tuner's settings (reference pitch, smoothing, tolerance and so on) into the generic tool-settings payload stored in a snapshot.

nodes.name: boundedPayloadNumber
nodes.summary: Reads a floating-point value out of a payload, rejecting non-finite or out-of-range values so a corrupted snapshot cannot poison settings.

nodes.name: boundedPayloadInteger
nodes.summary: Reads an integer out of a payload, rejecting values outside the permitted range.

nodes.name: decodeTunerPayload
nodes.summary: Rebuilds TunerSettings from a snapshot payload, falling back to AppDefaults for every field that is missing or out of bounds.

nodes.name: captureActiveWorkspace
nodes.summary: Captures the current workspace into a snapshot: each tool's presentation, bounds and settings payload, the layout tree and the focused tool.

nodes.name: applyWorkspaceSnapshot
nodes.summary: Restores a workspace snapshot: plans and executes the tool state changes, detaches the current containers, replaces the layout tree, recreates and re-presents each tool, then re-captures the resulting state.

nodes.name: setOperatingSystemFullscreen
nodes.summary: Applies fullscreen for the host platform: native full-screen on macOS, maximised borderless on Windows, and JUCE kiosk mode on Linux.

nodes.name: initialise
nodes.summary: JUCEApplication startup hook: parses the command line for automation flags and creates the MainWindow with the application name and version.

nodes.name: shutdown
nodes.summary: Releases the main window on application shutdown.

nodes.name: systemRequestedQuit
nodes.summary: Quits the application when the operating system requests it.

nodes.name: FeedbackInvitationPolicy.h
nodes.summary: Pure policy header deciding when to offer a feedback invitation, based on successful tool uses, prior dismissal, an opt-out flag and whether a live session is running.
nodes.languageNotes: constexpr free function over a POD State struct, so the rule is testable with no JUCE or UI dependency.

nodes.name: FeedbackInvitationPolicyTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 tests pinning FeedbackInvitationPolicy::shouldInvite: the use-count threshold, live-session suppression, and dismissal/opt-out suppression.

nodes.name: WorkspaceStartupSequenceTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 test asserting WorkspaceStartupSequence::run invokes workspace restore, window visibility and deferred audio in that exact order.

nodes.name: State
nodes.summary: Value type holding the feedback invitation counters and flags: successful uses, whether an invitation was already shown, and whether invitations are disabled.

nodes.name: shouldInvite
nodes.summary: Returns true only when no live session is active, no invitation was shown before, invitations are not disabled, and the successful-use threshold has been reached.

nodes.name: BenchmarkComparability.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements comparability validation between two benchmark run records, listing every field mismatch (scenario, workload, sample rate, buffer size, backend, build type, OS, CPU, instrumentation) that would make a comparison invalid.

nodes.name: display
nodes.summary: Anonymous-namespace helper that renders an optional/numeric field value as a human-readable string for mismatch reporting.

nodes.name: validateComparability
nodes.summary: Compares baseline and candidate run records field by field and returns a ComparabilityResult listing every material mismatch; runs are comparable only when the mismatch list is empty.

nodes.name: BenchmarkComparability.h
nodes.summary: Declares the comparability result value types and the validateComparability entry point used to decide whether two benchmark runs may be compared.

nodes.name: ComparabilityMismatch
nodes.summary: Value type naming a single field that differs between two benchmark runs, along with its baseline and candidate rendered values.

nodes.name: ComparabilityResult
nodes.summary: Result of a comparability check: a comparable flag plus the full list of field mismatches that caused rejection.

nodes.name: BenchmarkComparison.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements metric-level comparison of two benchmark runs, computing absolute and relative median changes for every metric present in either run once comparability has been established.

nodes.name: compareBenchmarkRuns
nodes.summary: Validates comparability first, then joins baseline and candidate metric summaries by metric id and emits per-metric absolute and relative percent changes; omits relative change when the baseline value is zero.

nodes.name: BenchmarkComparison.h
nodes.summary: Declares the per-metric comparison value types and the compareBenchmarkRuns entry point that produces a full benchmark comparison result.

nodes.name: MetricComparison
nodes.summary: Per-metric comparison record holding baseline and candidate values plus the derived absolute change and optional relative percent change.

nodes.name: BenchmarkComparisonResult
nodes.summary: Aggregate comparison outcome combining the comparability verdict, any mismatches, and the per-metric comparisons.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRecordCodec.cpp
nodes.summary: JUCE-var based serialization layer for benchmark run records: encodes the full record tree to JSON-compatible dynamic objects and decodes it back, performing schema-version migration and rejecting forward schema versions.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses juce::DynamicObject/juce::var as the JSON DOM; encode helpers live in an anonymous namespace and a templated encodeArray fans out per-item encoders.

nodes.name: toJuceString
nodes.summary: Converts a std::string to a juce::String via UTF-8, the shared adapter used by every encode helper.

nodes.name: encodeAudio
nodes.summary: Serializes an AudioConfiguration (device, backend, sample rate, buffer size) into a juce::var object.

nodes.name: decodeAudio
nodes.summary: Reconstructs an AudioConfiguration from its serialized juce::var representation.

nodes.name: encodeStringMap
nodes.summary: Serializes a string-keyed map (used for strategy parameters) into a juce::var object with one property per key.

nodes.name: decodeStringMap
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a string-keyed map by walking the properties of a serialized juce::DynamicObject.

nodes.name: encodeConfiguration
nodes.summary: Serializes a RunConfiguration including scenario, workload, strategy ids, strategy parameters, trial counts and nested audio configuration.

nodes.name: decodeConfiguration
nodes.summary: Reconstructs a RunConfiguration from serialized form, delegating to decodeStringMap and decodeAudio for nested structures.

nodes.name: encodeProvenance
nodes.summary: Serializes RunProvenance (version, commit, build type, OS, CPU, memory, audio, instrumentation) and maps the instrumentation overhead status enum to a stable string token.

nodes.name: decodeProvenance
nodes.summary: Reconstructs RunProvenance from serialized form and migrates older schema versions by defaulting an unknown instrumentation overhead status.

nodes.name: encodeTrial
nodes.summary: Serializes a TrialMeasurement including its epoch timestamp and duration in nanoseconds plus the nested metric sample array and event counters.

nodes.name: decodeTrial
nodes.summary: Reconstructs a TrialMeasurement, converting nanosecond integers back into chrono time points and durations and rebuilding the metric sample list.

nodes.name: encodeSummary
nodes.summary: Serializes a MetricSummary with its median, tail percentile, minimum, maximum and variability statistics.

nodes.name: decodeSummary
nodes.summary: Reconstructs a MetricSummary from its serialized statistics fields.

nodes.name: encode
nodes.summary: Top-level encoder producing the complete juce::var document for a BenchmarkRunRecord, including schema version, configuration, provenance, trial and summary arrays, warnings and optional status detail.

nodes.name: decode
nodes.summary: Top-level decoder that validates the schema version, rejects newer schemas, and rebuilds the entire BenchmarkRunRecord tree into a RecordDecodeResult.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRecordCodec.h
nodes.summary: Declares the record decode status enum, the RecordDecodeResult carrier and the static BenchmarkRecordCodec facade exposing encode/decode for benchmark run records.

nodes.name: RecordDecodeResult
nodes.summary: Carrier returned by decoding: a status, the optional decoded record, and a human-readable error string on failure.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRecordCodec
nodes.summary: Stateless static facade providing encode and decode of BenchmarkRunRecord to and from juce::var JSON documents.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRecordStore.h
nodes.summary: Declares the record store status enum, the StoredRecordResult carrier, the BenchmarkRecordStore class bound to a directory, and the free exportBenchmarkRecord function.

nodes.name: StoredRecordResult
nodes.summary: Carrier returned by load: a store status, the optional decoded record, and an error message.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRecordStore
nodes.summary: Directory-scoped store exposing save, load, listRunIds and the private fileFor path mapping for benchmark run records.

nodes.name: BenchmarkTypes.h
nodes.summary: Central schema header for the performance lab: defines the benchmark record schema version, the run/warning/overhead status enums, and every value type composing a BenchmarkRunRecord.
nodes.languageNotes: Header-only aggregate of plain-old-data structs; the schema version constant here gates codec migration and forward-version rejection.

nodes.name: BenchmarkWarning
nodes.summary: Warning attached to a run, pairing a WarningCode with a human-readable message.

nodes.name: AudioConfiguration
nodes.summary: Audio device settings captured for a run: device name, backend, sample rate and buffer size.

nodes.name: RunConfiguration
nodes.summary: The user-selected inputs for a benchmark run: scenario, workload and strategy ids, strategy parameters, warm-up and measured trial counts, and audio settings.

nodes.name: RunProvenance
nodes.summary: Environment provenance recorded with each run: application version, commit, build type, OS, CPU, memory, audio settings and instrumentation metadata.

nodes.name: MetricSample
nodes.summary: A single measured metric observation with its id, value and unit.

nodes.name: TrialMeasurement
nodes.summary: One measured trial: index, start timestamp, duration, metric samples and real-time event counters (deadline misses, dropouts, underruns).

nodes.name: MetricSummary
nodes.summary: Aggregated statistics for one metric across trials: sample count, median, tail percentile, minimum, maximum and variability.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRunRecord
nodes.summary: The complete persisted record of a benchmark run, composing schema version, run id, status, configuration, provenance, trials, summaries and warnings.

nodes.name: PerformanceLabController.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the performance lab UI state machine: validates configuration inline, drives run execution with progress and cancellation, and manages history, result/comparison selection, reopening and export while keeping state under a mutex.
nodes.languageNotes: State is guarded by a mutable std::mutex with an atomic cancellation flag, so setErrorLocked exists as the already-locked variant of setError.

nodes.name: PerformanceLabController
nodes.summary: Constructs the controller from injected validator, run executor, record loader and exporter callables and seeds the initial validation state.

nodes.name: state
nodes.summary: Returns a mutex-protected snapshot of the current performance lab state.

nodes.name: setConfiguration
nodes.summary: Replaces the run configuration, re-runs inline validation and clears any stale error.

nodes.name: startRun
nodes.summary: Validates the configuration, executes the benchmark through the injected executor with progress reporting and cancellation polling, then appends the resulting record to history and switches to the results view.

nodes.name: requestCancellation
nodes.summary: Sets the atomic cancellation flag and mirrors it into the observable state.

nodes.name: showConfiguration
nodes.summary: Switches the lab to the configuration view.

nodes.name: showHistory
nodes.summary: Switches the lab to the history view.

nodes.name: selectResult
nodes.summary: Selects a history entry as the active result, reporting a locked error when the index is out of range.

nodes.name: selectComparison
nodes.summary: Selects baseline and candidate history entries and computes their comparison, surfacing an error for invalid indices.

nodes.name: reopen
nodes.summary: Reopens a stored run by id through the injected record loader and appends it to history, reporting an error when no loader is configured or the run is missing.

nodes.name: exportSelected
nodes.summary: Exports the currently selected result to a destination via the injected exporter, reporting failures as locked errors.

nodes.name: setSafetyWarnings
nodes.summary: Stores externally supplied safety warnings on the observable state.

nodes.name: setError
nodes.summary: Acquires the state mutex and records an error message.

nodes.name: setErrorLocked
nodes.summary: Records an error message assuming the state mutex is already held.

nodes.name: PerformanceLabController.h
nodes.summary: Declares the performance lab view enum, the observable PerformanceLabState aggregate, and the PerformanceLabController whose validator, executor, loader and exporter collaborators are injected as std::function callables.
nodes.languageNotes: Dependencies are expressed as std::function aliases rather than abstract classes, which keeps the controller test-friendly without inheritance.

nodes.name: PerformanceLabState
nodes.summary: Observable snapshot of the lab: current view, configuration, validation result, progress, running/cancellation flags, safety warnings, history, selections, comparison and error.

nodes.name: PerformanceLabController
nodes.summary: Thread-safe controller coordinating configuration validation, run execution, history navigation, comparison and export for the performance lab.

nodes.name: PlatformProvenanceProvider.cpp
nodes.summary: Collects run provenance from the host platform, reading OS, CPU, memory and current audio device details through JUCE SystemStats and the audio device manager and normalising missing values to 'Unknown'.
nodes.languageNotes: Compile-time macros supply the application version, commit and build type, so provenance stays reproducible across builds.

nodes.name: knownOrUnknown
nodes.summary: Overloaded helper pair that substitutes the literal 'Unknown' for empty juce::String or std::string metadata values.

nodes.name: detect
nodes.summary: JUCE-backed platform probe returning OS name, CPU model, memory size and the current audio device's name, backend, sample rate and buffer size.

nodes.name: collect
nodes.summary: Assembles a RunProvenance from build-time constants and the injected metadata source, normalising every field through knownOrUnknown.

nodes.name: PlatformProvenanceProvider.h
nodes.summary: Declares the PlatformMetadata value type, the abstract PlatformMetadataSource interface, its JUCE-backed implementation, and the PlatformProvenanceProvider that turns metadata into a RunProvenance.
nodes.languageNotes: PlatformMetadataSource is a pure abstract interface with a virtual destructor, the seam that lets tests substitute a fake platform.

nodes.name: PlatformMetadata
nodes.summary: Value type holding the raw platform facts: operating system, CPU, memory bytes and audio configuration.

nodes.name: PlatformMetadataSource
nodes.summary: Pure abstract interface exposing detect(), the substitution seam for platform metadata acquisition.

nodes.name: JucePlatformMetadataSource
nodes.summary: Production PlatformMetadataSource implementation that reads real platform and audio device state via JUCE.

nodes.name: PlatformProvenanceProvider
nodes.summary: Adapter that composes build-time constants with a PlatformMetadataSource to produce a complete RunProvenance.

nodes.name: TrialAggregator.cpp
nodes.summary: Aggregates raw trial measurements into deterministic per-metric summaries (median, 95th tail percentile, min, max, population standard deviation) and totals the real-time event counters.
nodes.languageNotes: Rejects non-finite samples and inconsistent units by throwing std::invalid_argument, so aggregation failures are loud rather than silent.

nodes.name: median
nodes.summary: Computes the median of an already-sorted value vector, averaging the two middle elements for even counts.

nodes.name: populationStandardDeviation
nodes.summary: Computes the population standard deviation of a value vector as the variability measure for metric summaries.

nodes.name: aggregate
nodes.summary: Groups metric samples across trials, validating finiteness and unit consistency, then emits sorted MetricSummary entries plus totalled deadline misses, dropouts and underruns.

nodes.name: TrialAggregator.h
nodes.summary: Declares the trial event totals and aggregation result types plus the static TrialAggregator facade that turns trial measurements into metric summaries.

nodes.name: TrialEventTotals
nodes.summary: Totalled real-time incident counters across trials: deadline misses, dropouts and underruns.

nodes.name: TrialAggregation
nodes.summary: Aggregation output pairing the per-metric summaries with the totalled trial event counters.

nodes.name: TrialAggregator
nodes.summary: Stateless static facade exposing aggregate() over a vector of trial measurements.

nodes.name: BenchmarkComparabilityTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite that mutates one comparability-relevant field at a time and asserts validateComparability names exactly that mismatch, while confirming strategy differences remain intentionally comparable.

nodes.name: comparableRecord
nodes.summary: Test fixture builder producing a fully populated, self-comparable BenchmarkRunRecord used as the mutation baseline.

nodes.name: BenchmarkComparisonTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite covering compareBenchmarkRuns: absolute and relative median changes, preservation of metrics missing from one side, omission of relative change on a zero baseline, and blocking of incompatible runs.

nodes.name: recordWithSummaries
nodes.summary: Test helper that wraps a list of metric summaries into a comparable BenchmarkRunRecord.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRecordCodecTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite asserting the codec round-trips a fully populated record, migrates schema-version-one overhead status to unknown, and rejects forward schema versions.

nodes.name: BenchmarkTypesTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite pinning the default state of BenchmarkRunRecord to the current pending schema and verifying that configuration, provenance, trials and summaries compose as expected.

nodes.name: PerformanceLabControllerTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite driving the performance lab controller through inline validation, progress reporting with cancellation, reopen and export paths, and blocked comparisons of incompatible runs, using injected fake collaborators.

nodes.name: recordFor
nodes.summary: Test builder producing a BenchmarkRunRecord with a given run id, strategy id, median metric value and status.

nodes.name: validConfiguration
nodes.summary: Test builder producing a RunConfiguration that passes the fake validator.

nodes.name: PlatformProvenanceProviderTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite that substitutes a fake PlatformMetadataSource to assert the provider merges build-time platform facts with audio device metadata into a complete RunProvenance.

nodes.name: FakePlatformMetadataSource
nodes.summary: Test double implementing PlatformMetadataSource by returning a preset PlatformMetadata value.

nodes.name: TrialAggregatorTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite verifying deterministic aggregation statistics, even-sample medians with event totalling, metric ordering, rejection of inconsistent units, and empty results for no trials.

nodes.name: trial
nodes.summary: Test builder producing a TrialMeasurement with a given latency sample and event counters.

nodes.name: AppDefaults.h
nodes.summary: Header-only compile-time defaults for the application: settings schema version, default theme, unity input gain, and the tuner parameter presets (voice vs. general instrument).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `inline constexpr` namespace-scoped constants and `constexpr` factory functions so every default is resolved at compile time.

nodes.name: TunerSettings
nodes.summary: Plain aggregate holding the six tuner tuning parameters (display mode, easing, averaging, note-switch threshold, dropout frames, graph duration) shared by presets, persistence, and the tuner UI.

nodes.name: tunerPreset
nodes.summary: Returns the TunerSettings for a named preset — a steadier, more heavily averaged configuration for voice and the standard constants for general instruments.

nodes.name: tunerDefaults
nodes.summary: Convenience accessor returning the general-instrument tuner preset, used as the default tuner state throughout settings and the UI.

nodes.name: SettingsPersistence.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements load/store/clear for the application settings file, including schema-version migration, per-value range validation with fallbacks, corruption recovery, and encoding of the workspace catalog.
nodes.languageNotes: Validation helpers live in an anonymous namespace so only load/store/clearOwnedValues escape the translation unit; individual values degrade to defaults rather than rejecting the whole file.

nodes.name: hasOwnedSettings
nodes.summary: Reports whether the properties file contains any key owned by Practice Takes, so that a file holding only foreign keys is not mistaken for a migration candidate.

nodes.name: boundedValue
nodes.summary: Reads a numeric property and returns it only when finite and inside the given range, otherwise returning the supplied fallback.

nodes.name: loadTheme
nodes.summary: Decodes the stored theme integer into the Theme enum, falling back to the default theme for out-of-range values.

nodes.name: loadValidWindowBounds
nodes.summary: Parses a stored window-bounds string of four integer tokens with std::from_chars, rejecting malformed or non-positive geometry and re-serialising the validated rectangle.

nodes.name: loadFullscreenMode
nodes.summary: Decodes the persisted fullscreen mode enum, defaulting to normal windowed mode when the stored value is not a known member.

nodes.name: loadDisplayMode
nodes.summary: Reads the tuner display-mode integer and clamps unknown values back to the default display mode.

nodes.name: tunerPayload
nodes.summary: Serialises a TunerSettings struct into the versioned JSON tool-settings payload embedded in workspace snapshots.

nodes.name: migratedWorkspaceCatalog
nodes.summary: Builds a workspace catalog for legacy settings files by seeding the built-in Pitch Practice workspace with the user's migrated tuner settings.

nodes.name: recentTool
nodes.summary: Derives the legacy RecentTool enum from the catalog's focused workspace tool so older consumers stay consistent with the current workspace focus.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Loads the full settings State from a JUCE properties file, classifying the outcome as loaded, defaults, migrated, recovered-from-corruption, or newer-schema, and validating every field individually.

nodes.name: store
nodes.summary: Writes every owned settings key back to the properties file, including the encoded workspace catalog, and removes keys whose values are absent.

nodes.name: clearOwnedValues
nodes.summary: Removes only the properties owned by Practice Takes, leaving any third-party keys in the shared settings file untouched.

nodes.name: SettingsPersistence.h
nodes.summary: Declares the AppSettings namespace: the persisted State aggregate, the RecentTool/FullscreenMode/LoadStatus enums, and the load/store/clear entry points.

nodes.name: State
nodes.summary: The complete persisted application state — theme, microphone mute and gain, audio device state, tuner settings, per-tool window bounds, recent tool, fullscreen mode, and the workspace catalog — each member defaulted from AppDefaults or the built-in Pitch Practice workspace.
nodes.languageNotes: The workspaceCatalog member is initialised by an immediately-invoked lambda so its default is derived from WorkspaceBuiltIns rather than duplicated.

nodes.name: WorkspaceBuiltIns.h
nodes.summary: Defines the four immutable built-in workspaces (Pitch Practice, Vocal Warm-up, Spectrum Analysis, Performance Preparation) together with the tuner settings payloads they ship with.
nodes.languageNotes: The catalog is a function-local `static` initialised by a lambda, giving thread-safe lazy construction of the built-in definitions.

nodes.name: WorkspaceBuiltIns
nodes.summary: Static-only class exposing the immutable built-in workspace definitions and lookup by id; Pitch Practice acts as the universal fallback layout.

nodes.name: generalInstrumentTunerSettings
nodes.summary: Returns the versioned JSON tuner payload used by the instrument-oriented built-in workspaces.

nodes.name: voiceTunerSettings
nodes.summary: Returns the versioned JSON tuner payload tuned for voice — slower easing and heavier averaging — used by the Vocal Warm-up workspace.

nodes.name: pitchPractice
nodes.summary: Returns the Pitch Practice built-in workspace, the immutable single-tuner layout used as the fallback whenever a stored workspace cannot be recovered.

nodes.name: all
nodes.summary: Lazily constructs and returns the ordered vector of all four built-in workspace definitions, assembling each dock layout from WorkspaceNode leaves, splits, and tab groups.

nodes.name: find
nodes.summary: Linear lookup of a built-in workspace by its stable string id, returning nullptr when the id is not a built-in.

nodes.name: WorkspaceCatalogCodec.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements JSON encoding and defensive decoding of the workspace catalog, enforcing document size, name length, node depth and collection limits and recovering malformed layouts individually rather than rejecting the whole document.
nodes.languageNotes: Every read goes through typed helpers (readString/readInteger/readNumber) that reject wrong-typed or non-finite JSON values, so decoding is total rather than throwing.

nodes.name: toJuceString
nodes.summary: Converts a std::string_view into a juce::String using explicit UTF-8 decoding.

nodes.name: hasProperty
nodes.summary: Checks whether a JUCE dynamic object carries the named property, used as the guard before every field read during decoding.

nodes.name: readString
nodes.summary: Reads a JSON value as a non-empty string bounded by a maximum character count, returning false for wrong types or oversized input.

nodes.name: readInteger
nodes.summary: Reads a JSON int or int64 value, rejecting anything outside the range representable as a 32-bit int.

nodes.name: readNumber
nodes.summary: Reads a JSON numeric value as a double, rejecting non-numeric types and non-finite results such as NaN or infinity.

nodes.name: encodeBounds
nodes.summary: Encodes a WorkspaceBounds rectangle into a JSON object with x, y, width and height properties.

nodes.name: encodeNode
nodes.summary: Recursively encodes a dock-tree WorkspaceNode — leaf, tab group, or split with ratio and two children — into nested JSON objects.

nodes.name: encodeSnapshot
nodes.summary: Encodes a complete workspace snapshot: the dock root, the floating tool list with bounds, the focused tool, and the per-tool settings payloads keyed by valid JSON identifiers.

nodes.name: decodeBounds
nodes.summary: Decodes a JSON object into WorkspaceBounds, requiring all four integer geometry fields to be present and valid.

nodes.name: decodeNode
nodes.summary: Recursively decodes a dock-tree node while enforcing depth and node-count limits from the decode context, rebuilding leaves, tab groups and splits through the WorkspaceNode factories.

nodes.name: decodeSnapshot
nodes.summary: Decodes a full workspace snapshot — dock root, floating tools with bounds, focused tool, and tool settings payloads — returning nullopt when any required structure is malformed.

nodes.name: sourceExists
nodes.summary: Checks whether a workspace source id refers to a built-in workspace or to a named workspace that survived decoding, so dangling active-source references can be cleared.

nodes.name: encode
nodes.summary: Public entry point serialising a WorkspaceCatalog — version, active snapshot, active source and every named workspace — into a single JSON document string.

nodes.name: decode
nodes.summary: Public entry point parsing a catalog document into a WorkspaceCatalogDecodeResult, reporting tooLarge/invalid/newerSchema/loadedWithRecovery status, normalising each snapshot against the display areas, and falling back to Pitch Practice when the active layout is unrecoverable.

nodes.name: WorkspaceCatalogCodec.h
nodes.summary: Declares the workspace catalog serialization API: the decode status enum, the decode result aggregate, and the static encode/decode entry points together with the hard size limits they enforce.

nodes.name: WorkspaceCatalogDecodeResult
nodes.summary: Result of decoding a catalog document: a status (loaded, loadedWithRecovery, invalid, newerSchema, tooLarge), the optional catalog, and a human-readable error string.

nodes.name: WorkspaceCatalogCodec
nodes.summary: Static codec facade for workspace catalogs, capping documents at 4 MiB, named workspaces at 128, and workspace names at 80 characters.

nodes.name: WorkspaceDocuments.h
nodes.summary: The core workspace domain model: bounds, versioned tool settings payloads, the recursive dock-tree WorkspaceNode, floating tools, snapshots, named workspaces, and the catalog that owns them all.
nodes.languageNotes: WorkspaceNode implements a hand-written deep copy over unique_ptr children so snapshots remain value types with correct structural equality.

nodes.name: WorkspaceBounds
nodes.summary: Value type for an x/y/width/height rectangle used for floating tool windows and display-area constraints.

nodes.name: ToolSettingsPayload
nodes.summary: Opaque versioned settings blob a tool stores inside a workspace snapshot, letting each tool evolve its own serialization format independently.

nodes.name: WorkspaceNode
nodes.summary: Recursive dock-tree node that is either a leaf tool, a tab group with a selected tab, or an oriented split with a ratio and two owned children; provides deep copy, structural equality, and the three factory constructors.

nodes.name: FloatingWorkspaceTool
nodes.summary: Pairs a tool id with the screen bounds of its floating window in a workspace snapshot.

nodes.name: WorkspaceSnapshot
nodes.summary: A complete workspace state — dock root, floating tools, focused tool and per-tool settings — with helpers to derive whether a given tool is docked, floating or closed.

nodes.name: NamedWorkspace
nodes.summary: A snapshot given a stable identifier and a user-facing display name, the unit stored in the catalog and shipped as a built-in.

nodes.name: WorkspaceCatalog
nodes.summary: The persisted top-level workspace document: schema version, the active snapshot, the id of the workspace it came from, and the list of user-named workspaces.

nodes.name: leaf
nodes.summary: Factory constructing a leaf dock node that hosts a single tool id.

nodes.name: tabGroup
nodes.summary: Factory constructing a tabbed dock node from a list of tool ids and the currently selected tab.

nodes.name: split
nodes.summary: Factory constructing an oriented split node with a divider ratio and two owned child subtrees.

nodes.name: presentationOf
nodes.summary: Derives the canonical presentation of a tool from a snapshot — docked if it appears in the dock tree, floating if it has a floating entry, otherwise closed.

nodes.name: contains
nodes.summary: Recursively searches a dock subtree for a tool id across leaves, tab lists and both split children.

nodes.name: WorkspaceNormalizer.h
nodes.summary: Header-only recovery pass that turns an untrusted workspace snapshot into a valid one: resolving tool aliases, dropping duplicates and unknown tools, capping depth and collection sizes, repairing split ratios, and constraining floating bounds to real displays.
nodes.languageNotes: Reports what it had to repair via a WorkspaceNormalizationReport so callers can distinguish a clean load from a recovered one.

nodes.name: WorkspaceNormalizationReport
nodes.summary: Flags describing what normalization had to do: whether the fallback layout was used and whether depth or collection limits were exceeded.

nodes.name: WorkspaceNormalizationResult
nodes.summary: Pairs the normalized snapshot with the report describing the repairs that were applied.

nodes.name: WorkspaceNormalizer
nodes.summary: Static normalization engine enforcing the workspace safety limits — maximum dock depth, tabs, floating tools and tool-settings entries — and guaranteeing a usable snapshot for any input.

nodes.name: normalize
nodes.summary: Normalizes a whole snapshot: rebuilds the dock tree, deduplicates and bounds floating tools against display areas, drops settings for unknown tools, repairs the focused tool, and falls back to Pitch Practice when nothing usable remains.

nodes.name: normalizeNode
nodes.summary: Recursively normalizes a dock subtree, enforcing the depth limit, collapsing empty or single-child branches, deduplicating tabs, and clamping split ratios to a finite valid range.

nodes.name: normalizeLeaf
nodes.summary: Resolves a leaf's tool id through the registry (following aliases) and drops the leaf when the tool is unknown or already placed.

nodes.name: constrainBounds
nodes.summary: Clamps a floating window rectangle into the display area it overlaps most, so windows saved on a disconnected monitor reappear on a connected one.

nodes.name: pitchPracticeFallback
nodes.summary: Returns the built-in Pitch Practice snapshot used whenever normalization cannot salvage any layout.

nodes.name: WorkspaceSessionLifecycle.h
nodes.summary: Header-only policy for workspace state across application sessions: restoring a catalog at startup through normalization, capturing the active workspace at shutdown, and resetting the active workspace to the Pitch Practice built-in.

nodes.name: WorkspaceSessionLifecycle
nodes.summary: Static facade coordinating restore, capture and reset of the workspace catalog around application start and shutdown.

nodes.name: restore
nodes.summary: Restores a catalog for a new session by normalizing the active snapshot and every named workspace against the current display areas, dropping unrecoverable named entries and clearing a dangling active source, and reporting whether recovery was needed.

nodes.name: captureActive
nodes.summary: Stores the supplied snapshot as the catalog's active workspace so the live layout survives a restart.

nodes.name: resetActive
nodes.summary: Replaces only the active workspace with the Pitch Practice built-in, leaving the user's named workspaces intact.

nodes.name: sourceExists
nodes.summary: Checks whether an active-source id still refers to a built-in or a surviving named workspace after restore.

nodes.name: WorkspaceSnapshotApply.h
nodes.summary: Header-only two-phase application of a workspace snapshot to the live UI: a pure planning pass that validates placement and produces tool directives, and an execute pass that drives the caller's callbacks in a single coordinated rebuild.
nodes.languageNotes: Callbacks are injected as std::function members so the planner stays free of JUCE UI dependencies and remains unit-testable; a scoped RAII guard suppresses automatic saves during the rebuild.

nodes.name: WorkspaceSnapshotApply
nodes.summary: Static plan/execute pair with its supporting ToolBinding, ToolDirective, Plan and Callbacks types, converting a declarative snapshot into concrete layout nodes and tool presentation commands.

nodes.name: plan
nodes.summary: Builds an apply plan from a snapshot and the available tool bindings, rejecting the snapshot outright when a tool would be placed twice or docked and floated simultaneously.

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: Runs a plan against the caller-supplied callbacks — detach, replace layout, prepare and present each tool, rebuild once and restore focus — while suppressing automatic saves for the duration.

nodes.name: convertNode
nodes.summary: Recursively converts a persisted WorkspaceNode into a live WorkspaceLayoutState node, resolving tool ids through the registry and bindings and tracking placement to reject duplicates.

nodes.name: findBinding
nodes.summary: Linear lookup of the live tool binding for a resolved tool id, returning nullptr when the host provides no such tool.

nodes.name: WorkspaceToolRegistry.h
nodes.summary: Header-only registry of the workspace tools the application knows about, mapping canonical ids and their legacy aliases to a settings version so persisted layouts survive tool renames.

nodes.name: WorkspaceToolDefinition
nodes.summary: Describes one workspace tool: its canonical id, the historical aliases that should resolve to it, and the version of its settings payload.

nodes.name: WorkspaceToolRegistry
nodes.summary: Holds the tool definitions — defaulting to the built-in tuner, spectrogram and harmonic analyzer set — and resolves any id or alias to a canonical definition.

nodes.name: resolve
nodes.summary: Resolves a tool id to its canonical definition, first by exact id and then by scanning each definition's alias list, returning nullopt for unknown tools.

nodes.name: ThemeType.h
nodes.summary: Minimal header defining the Theme enum (light/dark) and the constexpr predicate used everywhere to branch on dark mode.

nodes.name: isDarkTheme
nodes.summary: Constexpr predicate returning whether the given Theme is the dark variant.

nodes.name: AppDefaultsTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite pinning the default constants: the general-instrument preset equals the tuner defaults, the voice preset tracks pitch more steadily, dark-theme detection distinguishes both themes, and input gain defaults to unity.

nodes.name: SettingsPersistenceTests.cpp
nodes.summary: The largest Catch2 suite in the batch, covering settings round trips, schema-one migration, corruption recovery, per-value fallback, newer-schema pass-through, tuner boundary validation, legacy recent-tool handling, and clearing only Practice Takes owned keys.

nodes.name: settingsOptions
nodes.summary: Builds the JUCE PropertiesFile options used by every test so each case reads and writes an isolated settings file.

nodes.name: TemporarySettingsFile
nodes.summary: RAII fixture creating a temporary settings file on construction and deleting it on destruction so persistence tests leave no residue.

nodes.name: WorkspaceBuiltInsTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite asserting the shape of each immutable built-in workspace — Pitch Practice as the tuner fallback, Vocal Warm-up's balanced split, Spectrum Analysis's larger spectrogram pane, Performance Preparation's selected tab — and that the catalog lists each exactly once.

nodes.name: WorkspaceCatalogCodecTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite for the catalog codec: deterministic structured round trips, rejection of malformed and unsupported documents, enforcement of document and named-workspace bounds, independent omission of malformed named layouts, and fallback from an unrecoverable active layout.

nodes.name: sampleCatalog
nodes.summary: Test fixture building a representative catalog with a split dock layout, tool settings and one named workspace, used as the round-trip subject across the suite.

nodes.name: WorkspaceDocumentsTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite verifying that workspace snapshots copy correctly and derive canonical tool presentation, and that catalogs keep stable named identifiers independent of user-visible display names.

nodes.name: WorkspaceRecoveryTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite for the normalizer's recovery behaviour: resolving aliases, removing duplicates, repairing structure, constraining split ratios, collapsing malformed branches, and falling back from an empty layout while reporting bounded input.

nodes.name: WorkspaceSessionLifecycleTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite covering startup and restart behaviour: first launch restores Pitch Practice, active topology and floating bounds survive capture and restart, floating windows are constrained to connected displays, missing tools are omitted, and reset replaces only the active workspace.

nodes.name: WorkspaceSnapshotApplyTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite for snapshot application: each tool is placed exactly once and carries only workspace state, duplicate dock or dock-plus-floating placement is rejected, and execution performs one coordinated presentation rebuild without mutating globals.

nodes.name: toolBindings
nodes.summary: Test fixture supplying the tool binding list the apply planner needs, standing in for the live UI's tool set.

nodes.name: Theme.cpp
nodes.summary: Defines the concrete light/dark colour values for the application, tuner and spectrogram palettes, plus the spectrogram level-to-colour ramp. Single source of truth for every colour the UI draws.
nodes.languageNotes: Free functions in a translation unit rather than a class; each palette is returned by value as a plain aggregate, so callers never hold theme state.

nodes.name: appPaletteFor
nodes.summary: Returns the full application chrome palette (background, panel, button, foreground, accent, warning, menu-bar gradient) for the requested theme.

nodes.name: tunerPaletteFor
nodes.summary: Returns the tuner-specific palette, including the dedicated in-tune indicator colour, for the requested theme.

nodes.name: spectrogramPaletteFor
nodes.summary: Returns the spectrogram chrome palette (background, panel, muted text, outline) for the requested theme.

nodes.name: spectrogramColourForLevel
nodes.summary: Maps a normalised 0..1 magnitude to a spectrogram pixel colour, using an HSV sweep in dark mode and an interpolated three-stop ramp in light mode. Clamps out-of-range levels.

nodes.name: Theme.h
nodes.summary: Declares the three palette aggregates (AppPalette, TunerPalette, SpectrogramPalette) and the free functions that build them per theme. Included by every themed UI component.

nodes.name: AppPalette
nodes.summary: Plain aggregate holding the eleven colours used by the application shell: background, panel, button and hover, foreground, muted, outline, accent, warning and the menu-bar gradient stops.

nodes.name: TunerPalette
nodes.summary: Plain aggregate of the eight colours the tuner draws with, including a dedicated in-tune highlight distinct from the generic accent.

nodes.name: SpectrogramPalette
nodes.summary: Plain aggregate of the four chrome colours used around the spectrogram image: background, panel, muted text and outline.

nodes.name: HarmonicAnalyzerComponent.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the harmonic analyzer tool: drains live microphone samples on a timer, feeds them to HarmonicAnalyzer, keeps a rolling history of harmonic magnitudes and spectral centroid, and renders bars plus history curves.

nodes.name: HarmonicAnalyzerComponent
nodes.summary: Constructor: stores the shared AudioInputService reference, marks the component opaque, registers itself as an audio listener and starts the repaint timer.

nodes.name: resetToDefaults
nodes.summary: Clears buffered audio, wipes the harmonic and centroid history buffers and repaints, returning the tool to its factory state.

nodes.name: audioInputStateChanged
nodes.summary: AudioInputService::Listener callback that translates the input state (disconnected, muted, clipping, active) into a user-facing error banner and drops stale samples.

nodes.name: timerCallback
nodes.summary: Per-frame tick: pulls a full analysis window from the audio FIFO, runs HarmonicAnalyzer::analyze on it, appends the result to history and repaints.

nodes.name: appendHistory
nodes.summary: Writes one analysis result into the fixed-capacity ring buffers for harmonic magnitudes and spectral centroid, advancing the write index.

nodes.name: harmonicColour
nodes.summary: Derives a distinct hue per harmonic index, adjusting saturation and brightness according to whether the active theme is dark.

nodes.name: paint
nodes.summary: Full render pass: draws the header and status text, the fundamental/centroid readouts, the per-harmonic magnitude bars with labels, and the scrolling history curves.

nodes.name: HarmonicAnalyzerComponent.h
nodes.summary: Declares the HarmonicAnalyzerComponent JUCE component, its audio-listener and timer bases, and the history buffers backing the harmonic display.

nodes.name: HarmonicAnalyzerComponent
nodes.summary: Final JUCE component that consumes the shared audio input, runs harmonic analysis on a timer and renders harmonic magnitudes plus a rolling history. Derives from juce::Component, AudioInputService::Listener and juce::Timer.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses private inheritance for the Listener and Timer mix-ins so the callbacks are implementation detail rather than public API.

nodes.name: SpectrogramComponent.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the scrolling spectrogram: windows and FFTs live microphone blocks, shifts the image left one column per frame, and paints a logarithmic frequency grid over it.
nodes.languageNotes: The waterfall is stored as a juce::Image and scrolled with moveImageSection, so only one new pixel column is computed per frame.

nodes.name: SpectrogramComponent
nodes.summary: Constructor: clears the waterfall image to the theme background, registers as an audio input listener and starts the refresh timer.

nodes.name: setTheme
nodes.summary: Switches the active theme and clears the accumulated waterfall image so no pixels rendered with the previous palette remain visible.

nodes.name: backgroundColour
nodes.summary: Accessor returning the current theme's spectrogram background colour.

nodes.name: panelColour
nodes.summary: Accessor returning the current theme's spectrogram panel colour.

nodes.name: mutedColour
nodes.summary: Accessor returning the current theme's muted text colour, used for grid labels and status messages.

nodes.name: outlineColour
nodes.summary: Accessor returning the current theme's outline colour used for the spectrogram border.

nodes.name: audioInputStateChanged
nodes.summary: Listener callback mapping the audio input state to a status banner and clearing the waterfall image when capture is no longer usable.

nodes.name: timerCallback
nodes.summary: Refresh tick: while a full FFT block is buffered, computes the next spectrogram column, then repaints once.

nodes.name: calculateNextColumn
nodes.summary: Reads one FFT-sized block from the audio FIFO, applies the Hann window and runs the frequency-only forward transform before handing off to the image update.

nodes.name: updateSpectrogramColumn
nodes.summary: Scrolls the waterfall image one pixel left, then writes the newest column by mapping each image row to a frequency, its FFT bin, decibel level and finally a colour.

nodes.name: maximumVisibleFrequency
nodes.summary: Returns the top of the displayed frequency range, clamped to the Nyquist limit of the current sample rate.

nodes.name: frequencyForImageRow
nodes.summary: Converts an image row index to a frequency using a logarithmic distribution between the minimum and maximum visible frequencies.

nodes.name: fftBinForFrequency
nodes.summary: Converts a frequency in Hz to the nearest valid FFT bin index for the current sample rate, clamping to the usable bin range.

nodes.name: colourForLevel
nodes.summary: Delegates normalised level-to-colour mapping to the shared theme ramp for the currently active theme.

nodes.name: yForFrequency
nodes.summary: Inverse of the row-to-frequency mapping: returns the vertical pixel position of a given frequency inside the spectrogram bounds.

nodes.name: frequencyLabel
nodes.summary: Formats a frequency for the axis, switching to a kHz representation above one kilohertz.

nodes.name: drawFrequencyGrid
nodes.summary: Overlays horizontal gridlines and labels at each decade-style frequency step that falls inside the visible range.

nodes.name: paint
nodes.summary: Draws the panel background, blits the waterfall image (or the audio error message when empty), strokes the border and finally the frequency grid.

nodes.name: SpectrogramComponent.h
nodes.summary: Declares the SpectrogramComponent along with its compile-time FFT/image constants and the displayed frequency and decibel ranges.

nodes.name: SpectrogramComponent

nodes.name: PitchDetector.h

nodes.name: availableSamples

nodes.name: push
nodes.summary: Producer side: writes a whole block with an optional gain, or drops the entire block and bumps the drop counters when it would not fit.

nodes.name: pop
nodes.summary: Consumer side: copies up to maximumCount buffered samples into the destination and advances the read position, supporting partial reads.

nodes.name: available
nodes.summary: Returns the number of samples currently buffered, computed from the atomic write and read positions.

nodes.name: discardPending
nodes.summary: Drops all buffered samples by moving the read position to the write position, deliberately preserving the drop diagnostics.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Full reset used when a consumer attaches or detaches: clears buffered audio and zeroes the drop counters.

nodes.name: droppedBlocks
nodes.summary: Returns how many complete callback blocks have been dropped because the FIFO was full.

nodes.name: droppedSamples
nodes.summary: Returns the total number of samples lost to dropped blocks.
