nodes.summary: Destructor that detaches the borrowed child components so they outlive the pane and are not deleted with it.

nodes.name: resized
nodes.summary: Component override that re-runs the stretchable layout over the two panes and the divider whenever the pane's bounds change.

nodes.name: currentRatio
nodes.summary: Computes the divider's current position as a clamped 0-1 fraction of the available split size, guarding against zero-sized panes.

nodes.name: moveDividerTo
nodes.summary: Programmatically repositions the divider, re-lays out the panes, and reports the resulting ratio to the workspace.

nodes.name: availableSplitSize
nodes.summary: Returns the pane extent along the split axis minus the divider thickness, floored at zero.

nodes.name: reportCurrentRatio
nodes.summary: Invokes the onRatioChanged callback with the freshly computed split ratio when a listener is attached.

nodes.name: WorkspaceTabBarButton.h
nodes.summary: Header-only tab button that turns a tab label into a workspace tool drag source once the pointer passes the drag threshold, while leaving the plain click-to-select path to the JUCE base class.
nodes.languageNotes: Overrides juce::TabBarButton mouse handlers and explicitly forwards to the qualified base implementation so default tab selection still works.

nodes.name: WorkspaceTabBarButton
nodes.summary: Final juce::TabBarButton subclass that arms on mouse-down, starts a workspace tool drag past the drag threshold or with Ctrl held, and dims itself while being dragged.

nodes.name: WorkspaceTabBarButton
nodes.summary: Constructor that forwards the tab name and owning bar to juce::TabBarButton and stores the drag handler callback.

nodes.name: paintButton
nodes.summary: Paints the tab using the base renderer, wrapping it in a transparency layer so a tab currently being dragged renders faded.

nodes.name: mouseDown
nodes.summary: Arms a potential drag on press and delegates to the base class so ordinary tab selection still occurs.

nodes.name: mouseDrag
nodes.summary: Starts the workspace tool drag once the pointer exceeds the drag distance threshold or Ctrl is held, resetting the button state so the click path is suppressed.

nodes.name: mouseUp
nodes.summary: Clears the drag flags on release and forwards to the base class only when no drag was started, so a drag never registers as a tab click.

nodes.name: WorkspaceTabbedComponent.h
nodes.summary: Header-only tabbed container that maps each tab to a WorkspaceLayoutState tool and builds draggable WorkspaceTabBarButton instances, reporting tab selection changes back to the workspace.
nodes.languageNotes: Drag handlers must be pushed before addTab() because juce::TabbedComponent::addTab calls createTabButton() synchronously.

nodes.name: WorkspaceTabbedComponent
nodes.summary: Final juce::TabbedComponent subclass that keeps a parallel vector of tool ids and drag handlers so tabs can be restored by tool and dragged out of the tab group.

nodes.name: WorkspaceTabbedComponent
nodes.summary: Constructor that forwards the tab-bar orientation to JUCE and stores the active-tool-changed callback.

nodes.name: addToolTab
nodes.summary: Records the tool id and its drag handler before delegating to addTab, suppressing the selection callback so restoring tabs does not look like a user action.

nodes.name: restoreActiveTool
nodes.summary: Selects the tab holding the given tool without firing the selection callback, used when rehydrating a saved workspace layout.

nodes.name: currentTabChanged
nodes.summary: JUCE override that maps the newly selected tab index back to a tool id and notifies the workspace, unless the change was programmatic.

nodes.name: createTabButton
nodes.summary: Factory override that constructs a WorkspaceTabBarButton wired to the drag handler recorded for that tab index.

nodes.name: WorkspaceLayoutState.h
nodes.summary: Pure, JUCE-free binary-tree model of the workspace tiling: leaves hold a single tool or a tab group, internal nodes are two-way splits, and drops on a pane edge subdivide that pane indefinitely.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately dependency-free header (only <algorithm>, <memory>, <optional>, <vector>) so the tiling engine is unit-testable without a JUCE message loop; nodes are owned via std::unique_ptr with recursive helpers.

nodes.name: WorkspaceLayoutState
nodes.summary: Owns the workspace's BSP tree of tools and exposes insertion by drop zone, removal with automatic collapsing, split-ratio and active-tab mutation, structural validation, and whole-tree layout commands.

nodes.name: makeLeafNode
nodes.summary: Static factory that allocates a leaf node holding a single tool.

nodes.name: makeTabsNode
nodes.summary: Static factory that allocates a tab-group node from a list of tools plus the initially active tab.

nodes.name: makeSplitNode
nodes.summary: Static factory that allocates a two-way split node with an orientation, ratio, and its two owned child subtrees.

nodes.name: dropZoneForPosition
nodes.summary: Maps a pointer position within a pane's rectangle onto a drop zone (left, right, top, bottom, centre, or float), defining the edge bands that trigger a split.

nodes.name: empty
nodes.summary: Reports whether the workspace tree currently has no root node.

nodes.name: contains
nodes.summary: Reports whether a given tool is currently tiled anywhere in the workspace tree.

nodes.name: replaceRoot
nodes.summary: Validates a candidate tree and, if it is structurally sound and free of duplicate tools, adopts it as the new root with freshly allocated node ids.

nodes.name: setSplitRatio
nodes.summary: Finds a split node by id and stores a finite, clamped divider ratio, used when the user drags a WorkspaceSplitPane divider.

nodes.name: setActiveTab
nodes.summary: Finds a tab-group node by id and records the selected tool as its active tab, rejecting tools that are not in that group.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Drops the entire workspace tree, leaving an empty layout.

nodes.name: insert
nodes.summary: Inserts a tool at a drop target, first removing any existing placement, then either seeding the root, appending to a tab group, or subdividing the target pane into a split.

nodes.name: remove
nodes.summary: Removes a tool from the tree, delegating to the recursive helper that collapses any nodes left degenerate.

nodes.name: applyLayoutCommand
nodes.summary: Applies an Arrange-workspace menu command by either flattening everything into one tab group or forcing the root split's orientation.

nodes.name: canSplitRoot
nodes.summary: Reports whether the root node is a split and can therefore have its orientation changed.

nodes.name: isRootOrientation
nodes.summary: Reports whether the root split currently uses the given orientation, used to tick the Arrange menu items.

nodes.name: isFlattenedTabs
nodes.summary: Reports whether the whole workspace has been collapsed into a single tab group.

nodes.name: allocateNodeId
nodes.summary: Hands out the next monotonically increasing node identifier for newly created tree nodes.

nodes.name: assignFreshIds
nodes.summary: Recursively stamps every node in an adopted subtree with a newly allocated id so restored layouts never collide with live ids.

nodes.name: validateNode
nodes.summary: Recursively checks an untrusted subtree for well-formed leaves, non-empty tab groups with a valid active tab, finite split ratios, and no duplicate tools across the tree.

nodes.name: findById
nodes.summary: Recursive depth-first lookup of a node by its identifier.

nodes.name: firstLeafOrTabs
nodes.summary: Walks down the leftmost branch of a subtree until it reaches a leaf or tab group, used as the default drop target.

nodes.name: find
nodes.summary: Recursive search for the node that currently hosts a given tool, matching both leaves and tab groups.

nodes.name: convertToSplit
nodes.summary: Rewrites an existing pane in place as a split node, moving its former contents into one side and the newly dropped tool into the other according to the drop zone.

nodes.name: removeRec
nodes.summary: Recursively removes a tool and collapses the tree afterwards: emptied tab groups and leaves vanish, single-tab groups degrade to leaves, and a split with one surviving child is replaced by that child.

nodes.name: collectLeaves
nodes.summary: Recursively gathers every tool in the tree in left-to-right order, flattening leaves and tab groups into one list.

nodes.name: flattenToTabs
nodes.summary: Collapses the whole workspace into a single tab group containing every tiled tool, preserving the leftmost tool as the active tab.

nodes.name: WorkspaceSnapshotCapture.h
nodes.summary: Header-only serializer that turns the live WorkspaceLayoutState tree plus per-tool presentation observations into a persistable WorkspaceSnapshot document, including floating bounds, tool settings, and the focused tool.
nodes.languageNotes: Stateless class of static methods bridging the JUCE-free layout tree to the WorkspaceDocuments value types.

nodes.name: WorkspaceSnapshotCapture
nodes.summary: Stateless helper exposing a ToolObservation input struct and static capture routines that walk the layout tree and emit a WorkspaceSnapshot.

nodes.name: capture
nodes.summary: Builds a WorkspaceSnapshot from the layout tree and tool observations, collecting floating windows and tool settings and only recording the focused tool when it is actually open.

nodes.name: captureNode
nodes.summary: Recursively converts a layout tree node into its WorkspaceNode document form, dropping tools that are not docked and collapsing splits or tab groups that lose all but one child.

nodes.name: findTool
nodes.summary: Looks up the ToolObservation matching a layout tool id, returning nullptr when the tool was not observed.

nodes.name: WorkspaceToolState.h
nodes.summary: Dependency-free state machine tracking whether a workspace tool is closed, docked, or floating, and reporting whether a transition needs a brand-new tool instance or can reuse the live one.
nodes.languageNotes: Header includes only <cstdint>, keeping the presentation state machine free of JUCE so it can be exercised in plain unit tests.

nodes.name: WorkspaceToolState
nodes.summary: Holds a tool's Presentation (closed/docked/floating) plus an instance generation counter, so dock/float moves keep the live tool alive while a close-then-reopen forces a fresh instance.

nodes.name: present
nodes.summary: Moves the tool to a target presentation and returns a Transition describing whether the presentation changed and whether a new tool instance must be constructed.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Transitions the tool to the closed presentation and reports whether that was an actual change.

nodes.name: presentation
nodes.summary: Returns the tool's current presentation mode.

nodes.name: isOpen
nodes.summary: Reports whether the tool is visible in any form, i.e. not closed.

nodes.name: instanceGeneration
nodes.summary: Returns the counter identifying the current tool instance, incremented only when reopening from closed.

nodes.name: MainComponentWorkspaceLayout.cpp
nodes.summary: MainComponent partial implementation that materialises the abstract WorkspaceLayoutState tree into live JUCE components, rebuilding split panes and tab groups on every layout change and positioning the resulting root.
nodes.languageNotes: Split-file member definitions for MainComponent; created containers are kept alive in workspaceContainers and detached explicitly before rebuild to avoid JUCE deleting borrowed dock panels.

nodes.name: setWorkspaceLayout
nodes.summary: Applies an Arrange-workspace command to the layout model and rebuilds the on-screen container hierarchy.

nodes.name: dockedTools
nodes.summary: Collects every tool whose presentation is docked and that has a live dock panel, used when enumerating what the workspace currently tiles.

nodes.name: buildWorkspaceNode
nodes.summary: Recursively turns a WorkspaceLayoutState node into JUCE components: a leaf resolves to its tool's dock, a tabs node becomes a WorkspaceTabbedComponent with drag-enabled tabs, and a split becomes a WorkspaceSplitPane wrapping its two built children.

nodes.name: detachWorkspaceContainer
nodes.summary: Tears down the previous workspace component tree, explicitly clearing tabs and reparenting borrowed dock panels so JUCE never deletes components the MainComponent still owns.

nodes.name: rebuildWorkspaceContainer
nodes.summary: Detaches the old container tree, rebuilds it from the current layout root, and makes the new root visible.

nodes.name: layoutWorkspace
nodes.summary: Positions the workspace root component inside the bounds left over after the title bar and chrome.

nodes.name: WorkspaceLayoutStateTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite covering the workspace tiling engine: drop-zone hit testing, repeated subdivision, tab grouping, removal and collapsing, split-ratio and active-tab mutation, and rejection of malformed restored trees.

nodes.name: WorkspacePresentationComponentsTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite verifying that the workspace split pane restores and reports its divider ratio, and that the tabbed component restores selection without replacing its draggable WorkspaceTabBarButton tabs.

nodes.name: WorkspaceSnapshotCaptureTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite checking that workspace capture records presentation, floating bounds, focused tool, and tuner settings payloads from a tiled layout tree.

nodes.name: observe
nodes.summary: Test helper that builds a WorkspaceSnapshotCapture::ToolObservation from an id, tool, presentation, and optional bounds and settings payload.

nodes.name: WorkspaceToolStateTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite asserting that dock and float transitions keep the live tool instance while a close-then-reopen cycle produces exactly one replacement instance.

nodes.name: __main__.py
nodes.summary: Package execution entry point that invokes the roadmap CLI's main() and propagates its exit code via SystemExit when the module is run with `python -m practice_takes_roadmap`.
nodes.languageNotes: Python `__main__.py` convention: makes a package directly runnable with `python -m`.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Central constants module defining the GitHub repository coordinates, the five roadmap stages, project field option sets, saved project view specifications, and title-matching patterns used for priority and tracker detection.

nodes.name: discovery.py
nodes.summary: Fetches the complete repository issue set from the GitHub GraphQL API using cursor pagination and maps each raw payload into a typed Issue model.

nodes.name: github.py
nodes.summary: GitHub integration layer wrapping the `gh` CLI and GraphQL API to create/read Projects v2 boards, manage custom fields, add issues, set field values, link sub-issues, and provision saved views.
nodes.languageNotes: Shells out to the `gh` CLI via subprocess rather than using an HTTP client, so authentication is inherited from the user's existing gh login.

nodes.name: main.py
nodes.summary: CLI orchestrator for the roadmap setup workflow: parses arguments, discovers and plans issues, provisions the GitHub Project with fields and views, assigns field values concurrently with caching, links sub-issues, and prints a summary report.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses ThreadPoolExecutor with as_completed plus a persisted fingerprint cache so repeated runs skip already-current field writes.

nodes.name: list_all_issues
nodes.summary: Pages through every repository issue with a GraphQL cursor query and returns a dict keyed by issue number containing fully populated Issue models, including milestone title and native parent linkage.

nodes.name: GitHubError
nodes.summary: Domain-specific exception raised whenever a `gh` CLI invocation fails, returns unparsable JSON, or a required command is missing.

nodes.name: Project
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass holding the identity of a GitHub Projects v2 board: its GraphQL node id, human-facing number, and web URL.

nodes.name: GitHubClient
nodes.summary: Facade over the `gh` CLI providing preflight checks, issue listing, project creation, item enumeration, single-select/date/iteration field provisioning, field value writes, sub-issue linking, and saved-view creation.
nodes.languageNotes: All network access funnels through run()/json() helpers that normalize subprocess failures into GitHubError.

nodes.name: log
nodes.summary: Prints a timestamped progress message with an immediate flush so long-running setup steps stream to the terminal in real time.

nodes.name: _normalize_field_value
nodes.summary: Recursively coerces an arbitrary project field payload (dict, list, or scalar) into a stable comparable string so live and desired values can be diffed reliably.

nodes.name: _current_field_value
nodes.summary: Looks up a project item's current value for a named field using case-insensitive matching and returns it in normalized form.

nodes.name: _values_match
nodes.summary: Compares a live field value against a desired value, treating a prefix match on date strings as equal so timestamped date fields do not trigger spurious rewrites.

nodes.name: FieldApplyResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass carrying the outcome of applying field values to one issue: the issue number, any failure messages, and the fingerprint to cache on success.

nodes.name: FieldAssignmentSummary
nodes.summary: Aggregated tally of a field assignment pass, splitting issues into failed updates, cache hits, already-current items, and those that required live API writes.

nodes.name: SetupResult
nodes.summary: Complete outcome of a setup run, bundling the target project, discovery and selection counts, missing/duplicate items, failed sub-issue links and views, the field summary, job count, and state file path.

nodes.name: parse_args
nodes.summary: Builds the argparse CLI surface covering repository owner/name overrides, project title, root issue, roadmap start date, job concurrency, status reset, force, and state file options.

nodes.name: configure_fields
nodes.summary: Idempotently provisions the project's custom fields — the Status single-select, each configured option field, the start and target date fields, and the iteration field — then re-reads the field list.

nodes.name: _add_one_issue
nodes.summary: Worker that adds a single issue to the project via a GraphQL mutation and returns the resulting ProjectItem; designed to be submitted to a thread pool.

nodes.name: add_issues_with_progress
nodes.summary: Adds all selected issues that are not yet on the board using a bounded thread pool, rendering a live progress bar and surfacing per-issue failures before re-reading the project items.

nodes.name: _desired_field_values
nodes.summary: Derives the target field values for an issue from its plan — stage, priority, estimate, target window, status, and ISO start/target dates — honouring the reset-statuses flag when deciding whether to overwrite an existing status.

nodes.name: _field_fingerprint
nodes.summary: Computes a stable hash over the project, item, plan and desired values so a subsequent run can detect that nothing changed and skip the API writes entirely.

nodes.name: _live_values_match
nodes.summary: Returns whether every desired field value already matches what the live project item reports, allowing the caller to record a cache hit without touching the API.

nodes.name: _apply_fields_for_issue
nodes.summary: Thread-pool worker that writes the single-select and date field values for one project item, skipping fields already matching, collecting failures, and returning a FieldApplyResult with the cacheable fingerprint.

nodes.name: assign_fields
nodes.summary: Drives the full field assignment pass over all planned issues: consults the persisted fingerprint cache, skips already-current items, dispatches remaining work to a thread pool with a progress bar, and continuously saves state as results land.

nodes.name: _link_one_subissue
nodes.summary: Thread-pool worker that establishes a native GitHub parent/child sub-issue relationship between two issue numbers.

nodes.name: ensure_subissues_with_progress
nodes.summary: Links every planned child issue to its parent concurrently, skipping links whose parent is outside the selected set, reporting progress, and accumulating the list of failed sub-issue relationships.

nodes.name: setup
nodes.summary: End-to-end setup pipeline: preflights the gh CLI, discovers all issues, selects descendants of the root tracker, plans schedules and stages, creates or reuses the project, adds items, configures fields, assigns values, links sub-issues, ensures views, and returns a SetupResult.

nodes.name: print_report
nodes.summary: Renders the human-readable end-of-run summary listing the project URL, discovery/selection counts, cache statistics, and any missing items, duplicate items, failed sub-issues, or failed views.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry function that parses arguments, acquires the exclusive state-store lock, optionally clears cached state, runs setup, translates GitHub and lock errors into non-zero exit codes, and prints the report.

nodes.name: models.py
nodes.summary: Dependency-free domain model module defining the frozen dataclasses shared by every other roadmap component: Issue, Stage, ProjectItem, and PlannedIssue.
nodes.languageNotes: All models are frozen dataclasses, making them hashable value objects safe to share across the thread pool.

nodes.name: planning.py
nodes.summary: Pure planning engine that parses parent/dependency markers out of issue bodies, classifies issues into roadmap stages, estimates sizes, assigns priority and status, and schedules start/target dates via topological ordering of the dependency graph.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses compiled module-level regexes plus a Kahn-style topological sort with deterministic tie-breaking so plans are reproducible run to run.

nodes.name: progress.py
nodes.summary: Self-contained terminal progress bar with exponentially smoothed ETA estimation, TTY detection, and interleaved message printing for long-running concurrent operations.

nodes.name: state.py
nodes.summary: Persistent cache and cross-process lock for roadmap runs, storing per-issue field fingerprints in an XDG cache JSON file written atomically and guarded by a PID-aware lock file.
nodes.languageNotes: Atomic saves via tempfile.mkstemp + os.replace, and stale-lock reclamation by checking whether the recorded PID is still alive with os.kill(pid, 0).

nodes.name: Issue
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass representing a GitHub issue with its number, GraphQL node id, title, body, URL, open/closed state, milestone title, and native parent issue number.

nodes.name: Stage
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass describing one roadmap stage: its display name, tracker-issue title prefix, target month window, and planned duration in weeks.

nodes.name: ProjectItem
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass pairing a GitHub Projects v2 item id with its backing issue number and the map of currently stored custom field values.

nodes.name: PlannedIssue
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass carrying the planner's decision for one issue: its stage, parent, dependencies, priority, estimate, status, and computed start and target dates.

nodes.name: next_monday
nodes.summary: Returns the upcoming Monday relative to today (or a supplied date), giving the roadmap a stable week-aligned start anchor.

nodes.name: parse_parent
nodes.summary: Extracts the parent tracker issue number from a `Parent tracker: #N` line in an issue body using a compiled regex.

nodes.name: parse_dependencies
nodes.summary: Scans `Depends on ...` lines in an issue body and returns the referenced issue numbers as a sorted deduplicated tuple.

nodes.name: parent_map
nodes.summary: Builds the issue-number to parent-number mapping, preferring GitHub's native parent link and falling back to the parsed body marker.

nodes.name: descendants_of
nodes.summary: Performs a breadth-first traversal of the parent/child issue tree from a root tracker and returns every reachable descendant issue number in sorted order.

nodes.name: tracker_stage
nodes.summary: Identifies whether an issue is itself a stage tracker by matching its title against each configured stage's tracker prefix.

nodes.name: milestone_stage
nodes.summary: Resolves an issue's stage from its GitHub milestone title, matching against both the stage tracker prefix and the stage display name.

nodes.name: stage_for_issue
nodes.summary: Determines an issue's roadmap stage by checking its own tracker prefix, then walking up the parent chain with cycle protection, and finally falling back to milestone-based inference.

nodes.name: estimate_size
nodes.summary: Parses an `Estimate: N-M days/weeks` marker from an issue body and buckets the effort into an XS/S/M/L/XL t-shirt size.

nodes.name: priority_for
nodes.summary: Assigns a Critical/High/Normal/Later priority based on configured critical title patterns, tracker prefixes, and dependency presence.

nodes.name: status_for
nodes.summary: Derives the initial board status for an issue from its open/closed state, whether it is a stage tracker, and title heuristics.

nodes.name: stage_ranges
nodes.summary: Lays the configured stages end to end from a start date and returns each stage's start and end date window.

nodes.name: _topological_order
nodes.summary: Kahn-style topological sort over the issue dependency graph with a deterministic ranking tie-break, appending any cycle-trapped remainder so no issue is lost.

nodes.name: plan_issues
nodes.summary: Top-level planner that groups issues by stage, topologically orders each stage by dependencies, spreads start and target dates within the stage window based on estimates, and emits a PlannedIssue for every issue.

nodes.name: _format_duration
nodes.summary: Formats a duration in seconds as a compact h/m/s string used for the progress bar's elapsed and ETA readouts.

nodes.name: ProgressBar
nodes.summary: Dataclass-based terminal progress bar that advances a counter, maintains an exponentially smoothed per-item rate for ETA, prints interleaved status messages, and degrades gracefully when the stream is not a TTY.

nodes.name: stable_hash
nodes.summary: Returns a deterministic SHA-256 hex digest for any JSON-compatible value by serializing with sorted keys and compact separators.

nodes.name: _cache_root
nodes.summary: Resolves the platform-appropriate cache directory, honouring an explicit override env var, Windows LOCALAPPDATA, and the XDG cache home with a home-relative fallback.

nodes.name: _pid_is_running
nodes.summary: Checks whether a recorded lock-holder process is still alive using a zero-signal os.kill probe, so stale lock files can be safely reclaimed.

nodes.name: StateLockError
nodes.summary: Exception raised when another roadmap setup process already holds the state store lock and the lock could not be acquired.

nodes.name: StateStore
nodes.summary: Persistent per-repository state store that loads and atomically saves field fingerprints, marks and forgets per-issue field currency, prunes stale entries, and exposes a context-managed exclusive lock.
nodes.languageNotes: The locked() contextmanager uses O_CREAT|O_EXCL for atomic lock acquisition and reclaims locks whose recorded PID is dead.

nodes.name: SettingsImportPersistence.h
nodes.summary: Header-only helper that atomically writes an imported SettingsTransferModel into the live juce::PropertiesFile, using a temporary file and overwrite-on-success so a failed import never corrupts the user's settings.
nodes.languageNotes: Static-only class used as a namespace; the whole implementation lives inline in the header so tests can exercise it without a translation unit.

nodes.name: SettingsImportPersistence
nodes.summary: Static utility class owning the settings-file write step of an import, plus the feedbackInvitationsDisabledKey property name shared with the settings UI.

nodes.name: persist
nodes.summary: Flushes the current properties file, stages the imported model into a temporary properties file, and overwrites the target only when the staged write succeeded; returns false on any failure so the caller can roll back.

nodes.name: SettingsImportTransaction.h
nodes.summary: Defines the two-phase settings import protocol: a stage step that reads and decodes a transfer document from disk, and an execute step that applies the candidate model with capture/apply/persist callbacks and rolls back on failure.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a private RAII ScopedSaveSuppression guard to disable automatic saving for the duration of the transaction and restore the prior flag on scope exit.

nodes.name: SettingsImportStageResult
nodes.summary: Result of the staging phase, carrying a SettingsImportStageStatus, the optionally decoded SettingsTransferModel, and a human-readable error message.

nodes.name: SettingsImportResult
nodes.summary: Outcome of executing an import, distinguishing cancelled, imported, applyFailed, persistenceFailed and rollbackFailed states along with an error message shown to the user.

nodes.name: SettingsImportTransaction
nodes.summary: Static coordinator for settings imports; exposes stage() and execute() plus a Callbacks struct that lets the UI layer supply capture, apply and persist behaviour without this header depending on the shell.

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: Applies a confirmed candidate model by capturing the prior state, applying the candidate and persisting it, restoring the captured prior state if either step fails and reporting rollbackFailed when even the restore fails.

nodes.name: stage
nodes.summary: Reads a settings transfer file into memory with a size cap, decodes it via SettingsTransferCodec, and maps decode outcomes onto cancelled/ioError/tooLarge/newerSchema/invalid staging statuses.

nodes.name: SettingsTransferCodec.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the JSON encode/decode of the whole application settings transfer document, including strict per-field type validation, schema version checks, theme and fullscreen enum parsing, and workspace-name validation against built-in reserved names.
nodes.languageNotes: Field readers are written as small anonymous-namespace helpers that return bool and write through an out-parameter, so decode() can accumulate validation failures uniformly across every field.

nodes.name: readInteger
nodes.summary: Reads a juce::var as an int, accepting both int and int64 representations and rejecting int64 values that fall outside the int range.

nodes.name: readNumber
nodes.summary: Reads a juce::var as a double from int, int64 or double variants and rejects non-finite results.

nodes.name: readBoolean
nodes.summary: Reads a juce::var strictly as a boolean, refusing to coerce numeric or string values.

nodes.name: readString
nodes.summary: Reads a juce::var strictly as a string, optionally rejecting empty values, and converts it to std::string for the transfer model.

nodes.name: parseTheme
nodes.summary: Maps a serialized theme name string back onto the application's theme enum, failing the decode when the name is unknown.

nodes.name: parseFullscreenMode
nodes.summary: Maps a serialized fullscreen mode name back onto the fullscreen mode enum, failing the decode when the name is unrecognised.

nodes.name: validateImportedWorkspaceNames
nodes.summary: Walks the workspace array of an incoming document and rejects it when a saved workspace name collides with a built-in workspace name or duplicates another entry, comparing on trimmed lower-cased names.

nodes.name: recentTool
nodes.summary: Derives the most recently used tool identifier from a decoded workspace catalog so the restored session reopens the same tool.

nodes.name: encodeWorkspaceCatalog
nodes.summary: Serializes the workspace catalog through WorkspaceCatalogCodec and re-parses the result into a juce::var so it can be embedded as a nested object in the settings document.

nodes.name: encode
nodes.summary: Builds the nested JSON document for a SettingsTransferModel — format marker, schema version, appearance, audio, window and workspace sections — and fails with tooLarge when the serialized output exceeds maximumDocumentBytes.

nodes.name: decode
nodes.summary: Parses and validates an untrusted settings transfer document: enforces the size cap and format marker, rejects newer schema versions, type-checks every field via the reader helpers, and reconstructs the workspace catalog before returning a SettingsTransferModel.

nodes.name: SettingsTransferCodec.h
nodes.summary: Public interface of the settings transfer format: the SettingsTransferModel data shape, encode/decode result types with status enums, and the SettingsTransferCodec entry points with the 4 MiB document size cap and format marker constant.

nodes.name: SettingsTransferModel
nodes.summary: The portable representation of a user's complete settings — schema version, originating application version, the persisted AppSettings state and the feedback-invitation opt-out — compared by value in tests via operator==.

nodes.name: SettingsTransferDecodeResult
nodes.summary: Decode outcome pairing a SettingsTransferDecodeStatus (loaded, invalid, newerSchema, tooLarge) with the optional decoded model and an error message.

nodes.name: SettingsTransferEncodeResult
nodes.summary: Encode outcome pairing a SettingsTransferEncodeStatus (encoded, invalidModel, tooLarge) with the optional serialized document and an error message.

nodes.name: SettingsTransferCodec
nodes.summary: Static codec facade declaring encode/decode and the maximumDocumentBytes and formatMarker constants that both the importer and the tests rely on to bound and identify transfer documents.

nodes.name: SettingsTransferFile.h
nodes.summary: Header-only writer that persists an encoded settings transfer document to a user-chosen file, writing through a temporary file and cleaning it up when the write or flush fails.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses juce::TemporaryFile so a partially written export never replaces an existing file on disk.

nodes.name: SettingsTransferExportResult
nodes.summary: Export outcome pairing a SettingsTransferExportStatus (exported, cancelled, ioError) with a user-facing error message.

nodes.name: SettingsTransferFile
nodes.summary: Static utility class exposing the single exportDocument entry point used by the settings UI to write a transfer document to disk.

nodes.name: exportDocument
nodes.summary: Treats an empty destination as a cancelled export, otherwise streams the document into a temporary file and only overwrites the destination once the write and flush both succeeded.

nodes.name: MainComponentSettings.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the MainComponent settings surface: the settings popup menu and window, settings import/export flows wired to the transfer codec, reset-to-defaults actions, and capture/save/load of the persisted application state.
nodes.languageNotes: All asynchronous JUCE callbacks capture a juce::Component::SafePointer<MainComponent> so a destroyed window cannot be dereferenced when a modal dialog or file chooser completes.

nodes.name: validWindowBounds
nodes.summary: Parses a stored bounds string and rejects it when the resulting rectangle is empty or implausibly large, guarding against restoring a window off-screen or at a corrupt size.

nodes.name: showSettingsMenu
nodes.summary: Builds the settings popup menu with theme, workspace and mute sub-menus and dispatches the selected item to showSettings, setTheme, toggleMuted or saveSettings.

nodes.name: showSettings
nodes.summary: Creates or re-focuses the settings window and wires each of its callbacks — preset, save, import, export, feedback and the four reset actions — to the corresponding MainComponent handler.

nodes.name: importSettings
nodes.summary: Launches an asynchronous file chooser, collects the current display rectangles, stages the chosen file through SettingsImportTransaction and either reports a staging error or moves on to confirmation.

nodes.name: confirmSettingsImport
nodes.summary: Summarises what the staged model will change — theme, audio, window and workspace counts — in an OK/Cancel alert and forwards the user's answer to executeSettingsImport.

nodes.name: executeSettingsImport
nodes.summary: Runs SettingsImportTransaction::execute with capture, apply and persist callbacks bound to captureSettingsState, applyTransferredSettings and SettingsImportPersistence::persist, then surfaces the outcome.

nodes.name: showSettingsImportResult
nodes.summary: Presents the import outcome as an info or warning alert, staying silent when the user cancelled.

nodes.name: exportSettings
nodes.summary: Captures the current settings state, encodes it via SettingsTransferCodec, then asynchronously asks for a destination and writes it with SettingsTransferFile::exportDocument, reporting encode or write failures.

nodes.name: applyTransferredSettings
nodes.summary: Applies a decoded transfer model to the live application — theme, mute, input gain, validated window bounds, saved audio device state and the workspace snapshot — acting as the apply callback of the import transaction.

nodes.name: resetCurrentTool
nodes.summary: Resolves the component backing the active tool and dispatches resetToDefaults to whichever of the tuner, spectrogram or harmonic analyzer it turns out to be.

nodes.name: resetAudio
nodes.summary: Unmutes, restores the default input device and refreshes the microphone warning banner.

nodes.name: resetLayout
nodes.summary: Resets the active workspace through WorkspaceSessionLifecycle, re-applies the resulting snapshot and saves the new settings.

nodes.name: resetAll
nodes.summary: Performs a full factory reset: default theme, reset audio, default tuner settings, resetToDefaults on every analysis tool, then a layout reset.

nodes.name: applyPreset
nodes.summary: Ensures the tuner tool is open and forwards the chosen preset to the TunerComponent.

nodes.name: captureSettingsState
nodes.summary: Snapshots the entire live application state — window and tool bounds, tuner settings, mute and gain, workspace catalog and audio device state — into the AppSettings structure used for both saving and exporting.

nodes.name: saveSettings
nodes.summary: Writes the captured settings state to the user properties file, honouring the automatic-save suppression flag unless the save was explicitly requested.

nodes.name: loadSettings
nodes.summary: Loads AppSettings at startup, applies audio and window state with bounds validation, and quarantines a corrupt properties file by moving it aside and re-storing defaults.

nodes.name: restoreLoadedWorkspace
nodes.summary: Restores the workspace catalog loaded from settings against the current display layout, falling back to a reset workspace and re-saving when the restore is rejected.

nodes.name: closeSettings
nodes.summary: Remembers the settings window bounds, destroys the window and refreshes the microphone warning.

nodes.name: MainComponentWorkspaceManagement.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements MainComponent's named-workspace commands — apply, save, rename, overwrite, delete and reset — as modal JUCE dialogs, plus the scripted UI validation scenarios used to drive those dialogs headlessly.
nodes.languageNotes: Dialog callbacks are scheduled with juce::ModalCallbackFunction and guarded by SafePointer, and the AlertWindow is released into the modal callback so its lifetime outlives the enclosing function.

nodes.name: workspaceStatusMessage
nodes.summary: Turns a workspace operation status and action verb into the user-facing success or failure sentence shown in the resulting alert.

nodes.name: showWorkspaceAlert
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper around juce::AlertWindow::showMessageBoxAsync used by every workspace command to report its result.

nodes.name: runUiValidationScenario
nodes.summary: Drives scripted UI validation scenarios on a delayed timer — applying built-in workspaces, exercising the save dialog and text editor, and replaying settings-import confirmation and restore paths without user interaction.

nodes.name: applyWorkspace
nodes.summary: Applies a workspace by id, reports failures through showWorkspaceResult, then re-applies the resulting snapshot and persists the new active workspace.

nodes.name: showSaveWorkspaceDialog
nodes.summary: Builds a modal AlertWindow with a length-restricted name editor and forwards the entered name to saveNamedWorkspace when the user confirms.

nodes.name: showRenameWorkspaceDialog
nodes.summary: Refuses to open unless a named workspace is active, otherwise presents a pre-filled rename dialog and hands the new name to renameNamedWorkspace.

nodes.name: saveNamedWorkspace
nodes.summary: Captures the active workspace and saves it under the given name, prompting for overwrite confirmation and re-entering itself with confirmed=true when the user agrees.

nodes.name: renameNamedWorkspace
nodes.summary: Renames the active named workspace, asking for confirmation when the new name collides with an existing one and re-entering itself once confirmed.

nodes.name: confirmOverwriteWorkspace
nodes.summary: Asks the user to confirm overwriting the active named workspace with the current layout, then captures and overwrites it.

nodes.name: confirmDeleteWorkspace
nodes.summary: Asks the user to confirm deleting the active named workspace and removes it from the catalog on approval.

nodes.name: confirmResetWorkspace
nodes.summary: Asks the user to confirm discarding the current layout and delegates to resetLayout before reporting the result.

nodes.name: showWorkspaceResult
nodes.summary: Central result handler for workspace commands: saves settings on success, formats the status message, and shows the appropriate info or warning alert including the requested name when relevant.

nodes.name: SettingsTransferCodecTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite covering the settings transfer stack end to end: encode/decode round-trips and determinism, oversized and malformed document rejection, schema version handling, workspace name collision rules, file export failure cleanup, and import transaction rollback and persistence behaviour.
nodes.languageNotes: RAII fixtures (TemporarySettingsFile, TemporaryTransferDirectory) create and delete real files on disk so the codec and exporter are exercised against genuine filesystem failures rather than mocks.

nodes.name: TemporarySettingsFile
nodes.summary: RAII fixture that creates a temp file for properties-file tests and deletes it in the destructor.

nodes.name: TemporaryTransferDirectory
nodes.summary: RAII fixture that creates a unique temp directory for transfer-file export tests and recursively removes it afterwards.

nodes.name: settingsOptions
nodes.summary: Builds the juce::PropertiesFile::Options used by the persistence tests so they write to an isolated temporary location.

nodes.name: encodedDocument
nodes.summary: Encodes a model through SettingsTransferCodec and asserts the encode succeeded, returning the document string for tests that need valid input.

nodes.name: HarmonicAnalyzer.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the harmonic analysis DSP pass: runs pitch detection, applies a Hann-windowed FFT, then extracts per-harmonic amplitudes, spectral centroid, inharmonicity and a pitched-confidence score.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses juce::dsp::FFT with a fixed-order (2^12) real transform and std::span with a compile-time extent so the window size is checked at compile time.

nodes.name: HarmonicAnalyzer.h
nodes.summary: Declares the HarmonicAnalyzer class and its Result struct, defining the harmonic-profile contract (fundamental, centroid, confidence, inharmonicity, relative amplitudes) consumed by the harmonics UI and benchmarks.

nodes.name: HarmonicAnalysisActions.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the production benchmark actions that drive the real HarmonicAnalyzer over a synthetic two-partial 220 Hz fixture and count how many frames were reported as pitched.

nodes.name: HarmonicAnalysisActions.h
nodes.summary: Declares HarmonicAnalysisActions, the concrete SustainedAudioAnalysisActions implementation that owns a HarmonicAnalyzer and its generated sample fixture for benchmark runs.

nodes.name: SustainedAudioAnalysisScenario.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the sustained-audio-analysis benchmark scenario: validates the run configuration against expected scenario/workload ids and audio settings, then delegates prepare/run/verify/restore to the injected actions abstraction.

nodes.name: SustainedAudioAnalysisScenario.h
nodes.summary: Declares the SustainedAudioAnalysisActions pure-virtual seam and the SustainedAudioAnalysisScenario BenchmarkScenario implementation that runs a fixed frame count through it.
nodes.languageNotes: Defines an abstract-base seam (pure virtual methods plus virtual destructor) so the scenario can be exercised with a test fake without pulling in real DSP.

nodes.name: HarmonicAnalyzerTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite for HarmonicAnalyzer covering relative harmonic amplitudes, weak fundamentals, spectral centroid brightness, noise rejection, and a tagged per-frame throughput benchmark at 48 kHz and 44.1 kHz.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Catch2 BENCHMARK blocks behind the hidden `[.benchmark]` tag so throughput measurements do not run in the default test pass.

nodes.name: SustainedAudioAnalysisScenarioTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite for SustainedAudioAnalysisScenario that verifies the scenario drives its actions seam in order using a fake, and that the real HarmonicAnalysisActions reports the expected pitched-frame count end to end.

nodes.name: analyze
nodes.summary: Produces a full harmonic Result for one window of samples: detects the fundamental, FFTs the windowed buffer, sums the spectrum for the centroid, picks a peak bin near each of the eight expected harmonics, then derives inharmonicity and a clamped confidence used to set isPitched.

nodes.name: HarmonicAnalyzer
nodes.summary: Stateful harmonic analyzer that owns a PitchDetector, a 4096-point FFT and a Hann window, and exposes a single analyze() entry point returning an eight-partial harmonic profile.

nodes.name: prepareAnalysis
nodes.summary: Resets the pitched-frame counter and regenerates the deterministic sample fixture before a benchmark trial.

nodes.name: analyzeFixture
nodes.summary: Runs the generated fixture through HarmonicAnalyzer::analyze once per requested frame, incrementing the pitched-frame counter for each result flagged as pitched.

nodes.name: pitchedFrameCount
nodes.summary: Returns the number of analyzed frames that the analyzer reported as pitched, used by the scenario's correctness check.

nodes.name: restoreAnalysis
nodes.summary: Clears the pitched-frame counter so the actions object returns to its pre-trial state.

nodes.name: generateFixture
nodes.summary: Fills the sample buffer with a deterministic 220 Hz tone plus a half-amplitude second partial so every benchmark run analyzes identical audio.

nodes.name: HarmonicAnalysisActions
nodes.summary: Production implementation of the SustainedAudioAnalysisActions seam that owns a HarmonicAnalyzer and a window-sized fixture buffer, letting the benchmark scenario exercise real DSP.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Checks a RunConfiguration against this scenario, collecting errors for a mismatched scenario id or workload id, a non-positive sample rate, a zero buffer size, and a zero frame count.

nodes.name: prepare
nodes.summary: Delegates trial setup to the injected actions by calling prepareAnalysis().

nodes.name: runTrial
nodes.summary: Executes one measured trial by asking the actions to analyze the configured number of fixture frames.

nodes.name: verifyCorrectness
nodes.summary: Confirms the actions reported a pitched frame for every analyzed frame, returning a ValidationResult failure when the counts diverge.

nodes.name: restore
nodes.summary: Returns the workload to its baseline state by delegating to the actions' restoreAnalysis().

nodes.name: SustainedAudioAnalysisActions
nodes.summary: Pure-virtual seam describing the semantic steps of the sustained audio workload (prepare, analyze frames, report pitched frames, restore) so the scenario can run against real DSP or a test fake.

nodes.name: SustainedAudioAnalysisScenario
nodes.summary: BenchmarkScenario implementation for the sustained-audio-analysis workload, holding a reference to its actions seam and the frame count (default 64) analyzed per trial.

nodes.name: harmonicSignal
nodes.summary: Test helper that synthesizes a window of samples by summing four sine partials at the given relative amplitudes over a 200 Hz fundamental.

nodes.name: FakeAnalysisActions
nodes.summary: In-test fake implementing SustainedAudioAnalysisActions that records prepare/restore flags and accumulates analyzed and pitched frame counts without doing any DSP.

nodes.name: validConfiguration
nodes.summary: Builds a RunConfiguration matching the scenario's expected ids and 48 kHz / 256-frame audio settings for the validation test.

nodes.name: NamedWorkspaceService.h
nodes.summary: Header-only service implementing the full lifecycle of user-named workspace layouts — save, apply, rename, overwrite and delete — against a WorkspaceCatalog, with name validation, reserved-name protection against built-ins, and collision-free ID generation.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure header-only C++ class with no JUCE dependency, which is what makes it directly unit-testable under Catch2; all mutation goes through a Result/ResultStatus enum instead of exceptions, and confirmation-required flows are expressed as a status rather than a callback.

nodes.name: NamedWorkspaceService
nodes.summary: Stateless workspace-catalog manipulator exposing save/apply/rename/overwrite/remove operations that return a Result carrying a ResultStatus and the affected workspace ID. Enforces a 80-character name limit and a 128-workspace catalog cap.

nodes.name: NamedWorkspaceService
nodes.summary: Explicit constructor accepting an injectable IdGenerator, defaulting to the random hex generator, so tests can substitute deterministic IDs.

nodes.name: save
nodes.summary: Saves the catalog's active snapshot under a new name, validating the name, requesting confirmation on a name collision, rejecting when the catalog is full, and assigning a freshly generated unique ID.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Activates a workspace by ID, resolving first against the built-in presets and then against the named catalog entries, copying its snapshot into the catalog's active layout.

nodes.name: rename
nodes.summary: Renames a named workspace after rejecting built-in IDs as immutable, validating the new name, and prompting for confirmation when another entry already holds that name (which it then erases).

nodes.name: overwrite
nodes.summary: Replaces an existing named workspace's stored snapshot with the catalog's current active layout, gated behind a confirmation flag and refusing built-in entries.

nodes.name: remove
nodes.summary: Deletes a named workspace after confirmation, refusing built-in IDs, and clears the catalog's activeSource when the deleted entry was the active one.

nodes.name: defaultIdGenerator
nodes.summary: Builds the default IdGenerator closure, seeding a random engine from std::random_device and emitting zero-padded hexadecimal identifiers.

nodes.name: prepareName
nodes.summary: Normalises and validates a candidate workspace name — treating nullopt as cancellation, trimming whitespace, enforcing the UTF-8 character limit, and rejecting names reserved by built-in presets.

nodes.name: trim
nodes.summary: Strips leading and trailing whitespace from a string_view using an unsigned-char-safe isspace predicate.

nodes.name: utf8CharacterCount
nodes.summary: Counts UTF-8 code points by ignoring continuation bytes, so the name-length limit applies to characters rather than raw bytes.

nodes.name: folded
nodes.summary: Produces a lowercase-folded copy of a string used as the comparison key for case-insensitive workspace-name matching.

nodes.name: isReservedName
nodes.summary: Reports whether a candidate name case-insensitively collides with any built-in workspace preset name, which the service treats as reserved.

nodes.name: findNamedById
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator to the named workspace with the given ID, or the catalog's end iterator when absent.

nodes.name: findNamedByName
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator to the named workspace whose case-folded name matches the given name, used to detect naming collisions.

nodes.name: uniqueId
nodes.summary: Draws IDs from the injected generator until one collides with neither an existing named workspace nor a built-in preset, giving up after a bounded number of attempts.

nodes.name: WorkspaceMenuModel.h
nodes.summary: Defines the UI-agnostic view model for the Workspaces popup menu, projecting a WorkspaceCatalog into an ordered entry list plus the enabled/disabled state of the Save As, Overwrite, Rename and Delete actions.
nodes.languageNotes: Keeps all menu decision logic in a plain struct free of JUCE types, so the menu's enablement rules can be unit-tested without constructing a UI component.

nodes.name: WorkspaceMenuEntry
nodes.summary: Value struct describing one row of the Workspaces menu: its ID, display name, whether it is a built-in preset, and whether it is currently selected.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a defaulted operator== (C++20) so tests can compare whole entries against brace-initialised literals.

nodes.name: WorkspaceMenuModel
nodes.summary: Aggregate holding the ordered menu entries alongside four boolean action-enablement flags, constructed exclusively through its static fromCatalog factory.

nodes.name: fromCatalog
nodes.summary: Projects a WorkspaceCatalog into a menu model by listing built-in presets before named workspaces, marking the active source as selected, disabling Save As at the catalog cap, and enabling Overwrite/Rename/Delete only when the active workspace is a named entry.

nodes.name: MainComponentWorkspaceMenu.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements MainComponent's Tools popup menu, assembling the tuner, spectrogram, harmonic-analyzer, layout and workspace submenus from current state and dispatching the selected item ID back to the owning component's tool, layout and workspace commands.
nodes.languageNotes: Menu item IDs are file-local constexpr constants in an anonymous namespace and the async callback captures a juce::Component::SafePointer<MainComponent>, so a menu selection arriving after the component is destroyed is safely dropped. The Performance Lab entries are compiled out entirely unless PRACTICE_TAKES_ENABLE_PERFORMANCE_LAB is defined.

nodes.name: showToolsMenu
nodes.summary: Builds and asynchronously shows the complete Tools popup menu, then routes the chosen item ID to openTool, presentTool, closeTool, setWorkspaceLayout, applyWorkspace or one of the workspace dialog commands.

nodes.name: showPerformanceLab
nodes.summary: Lazily creates the Performance Lab window with the current theme palette on first use, or brings the existing window to front on subsequent invocations.

nodes.name: automatePerformanceLab
nodes.summary: Recreates the Performance Lab window in automated mode with a completion callback, used to drive benchmark runs headlessly rather than through user interaction.

nodes.name: closePerformanceLab
nodes.summary: Destroys the Performance Lab window by resetting its owning unique_ptr; passed as the window's own close callback.

nodes.name: NamedWorkspaceServiceTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite covering NamedWorkspaceService end to end: name trimming and stable ID assignment on save, cancellation, collision confirmation, reserved built-in names, rename and overwrite semantics, and deletion clearing the active source.
nodes.languageNotes: Injects a deterministic IdGenerator lambda into the service constructor so generated workspace IDs are assertable rather than random.

nodes.name: catalogWithNamedWorkspace
nodes.summary: Test fixture helper building a WorkspaceCatalog whose active layout is the performance-preparation preset and which already contains one saved 'Saved Spectrum' named workspace.

nodes.name: WorkspaceMenuModelTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite verifying WorkspaceMenuModel::fromCatalog — that built-ins precede named workspaces with correct selection, that Overwrite/Rename/Delete are disabled for built-in and edited layouts, and that Save As is disabled once the catalog reaches NamedWorkspaceService::maximumNamedWorkspaces.

nodes.name: ApplicationLaunchTimer.h
nodes.summary: Declares the performance::ApplicationLaunchTimer class that measures elapsed time from process start to first main-window visibility, plus two free functions exposing a process-wide singleton instance.
nodes.languageNotes: Header-only declaration using std::chrono::steady_clock and std::optional; default arguments (Clock::now()) let callers omit explicit timestamps in production while tests inject deterministic time points.

nodes.name: ApplicationLaunchTimer.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the launch-timing class and hosts an anonymous-namespace singleton timer that the free markMainWindowVisible() and applicationLaunchDuration() functions delegate to.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses an unnamed-namespace global to give the translation unit internal linkage for the shared timer, so the free functions form the only public seam onto that state.

nodes.name: ApplicationLaunchTimerTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 test cases verifying that ApplicationLaunchTimer computes the interval to first window visibility and that repeated marks preserve the earliest timestamp.
nodes.languageNotes: Injects a default-constructed TimePoint as a synthetic epoch so durations are exact and independent of wall-clock timing.

nodes.name: ApplicationLaunchTimer
nodes.summary: Records a process start time point and latches the duration until the main window first becomes visible, exposing it as an optional that stays empty until marked.

nodes.name: ApplicationLaunchTimer::ApplicationLaunchTimer
nodes.summary: Constructs the timer by capturing the supplied process start time point, defaulting to the current steady-clock reading.

nodes.name: ApplicationLaunchTimer::markMainWindowVisible
nodes.summary: Latches the launch duration as the difference between the visible timestamp and process start, ignoring subsequent calls so the first visibility wins.

nodes.name: ApplicationLaunchTimer::duration
nodes.summary: Returns the latched launch duration, or an empty optional when the main window has not yet been marked visible.

nodes.name: markMainWindowVisible
nodes.summary: Free namespace-level entry point that marks the process-wide launch timer as having shown its main window; called by the bootstrap window startup sequence.

nodes.name: applicationLaunchDuration
nodes.summary: Free namespace-level accessor returning the process-wide launch-to-main-window duration, consumed by the performance lab to report a launch summary metric.

nodes.name: benchmarks.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that builds PracticeTakes in Release mode on Ubuntu, runs the Catch2 [.benchmark] DSP suite to benchmark.xml, probes application startup wall time, and renders a step summary via scripts/quality/format_benchmarks.py. Runs on pushes to main touching src/tests/cmake, weekly on Monday 04:00 UTC, and on demand.
nodes.languageNotes: Startup timing is measured inline with `timeout 5s` plus nanosecond `date` arithmetic because the binary is expected to exit non-zero on a headless CI runner with no audio device.

nodes.name: clang-tidy-main.yml
nodes.summary: Post-merge workflow that applies safe clang-tidy fix-its to every src/**.cpp on main, reformats the edits with clang-format, re-validates the build and remaining findings, then commits and pushes the automatic fixes back to main as github-actions[bot].
nodes.languageNotes: Shares the concurrency group 'practice-takes-main-quality-and-release' with release.yml so auto-fix commits never race a release, and self-skips when the actor is github-actions[bot] to avoid an infinite push loop.

nodes.name: cpp-quality-check.yml
nodes.summary: Pull-request gate that generates the JUCE headers and compilation database, verifies clang-format compliance across all src/ sources and headers, and runs clang-tidy through scripts/quality/run_clang_tidy.py. Fails loudly if zero .cpp files are discovered rather than reporting a vacuous pass.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses ccache with a per-SHA cache key and restore-keys prefix fallback so the JUCE header generation build stays cheap across PR pushes.

nodes.name: 0001_initial.sql
nodes.summary: Baseline D1/SQLite migration creating the feedback-intake core schema: authorization_requests (rate-limit ledger), consumed_authorizations (one-shot token replay guard), and feedback_submissions (the submission record keyed by receipt_id), plus lookup indexes on client_hash and installation_hash.
nodes.languageNotes: SQLite/Cloudflare D1 dialect: INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT rowid keys and epoch-integer timestamps rather than native DATETIME types.

nodes.name: authorization_requests
nodes.summary: Append-only ledger of authorization token requests keyed by client_hash and request timestamp, used to enforce per-client submission rate limits.

nodes.name: consumed_authorizations
nodes.summary: Replay-protection table recording each authorization token_id once it has been redeemed, so a single-use token cannot be spent twice.

nodes.name: feedback_submissions
nodes.summary: Primary table storing every accepted user feedback submission — receipt id, schema version, app version, hashed installation/client identity, category, message body and optional contact email. Extended by every later migration in this directory.

nodes.name: 0002_admin_triage.sql
nodes.summary: Adds the admin triage workflow columns to feedback_submissions — constrained status, developer_notes, priority, tags_json, github_issue_url and a self-referential duplicate_of foreign key — with indexes supporting status-ordered and category/version triage queries.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses CHECK (col IN (...)) constraints as a lightweight enum substitute, since SQLite has no native enum type.

nodes.name: 0003_admin_action_receipts.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the admin_action_receipts audit table recording every create/update/delete an admin performs against a submission, along with three descending-time indexes for the audit log views.

nodes.name: admin_action_receipts
nodes.summary: Immutable audit log of administrative mutations, capturing the acting admin_email, the action verb, the affected receipt_id and a JSON details blob describing the change.

nodes.name: 0004_optional_screenshots.sql
nodes.summary: Two-line migration adding optional screenshot_mime_type and screenshot_base64 columns to feedback_submissions so users can attach an image to a report.

nodes.name: 0005_idempotent_submissions.sql
nodes.summary: Adds client_submission_id to feedback_submissions and a partial UNIQUE index over (installation_hash, client_submission_id), making retried submissions idempotent while still allowing unlimited NULL-id legacy rows.
nodes.languageNotes: Partial index with a WHERE clause — the uniqueness constraint applies only to non-NULL client_submission_id values, which is how SQLite expresses a conditional unique key.

nodes.name: 0006_operations.sql
nodes.summary: Operational-hardening migration adding quarantine columns to feedback_submissions and creating two new tables: request_metrics (hourly per-route latency/outcome rollups) and maintenance_runs (retention job execution log).

nodes.name: request_metrics
nodes.summary: Pre-aggregated hourly request telemetry keyed by (hour, route, outcome), tracking request counts plus total and maximum duration for the authorizations and submissions endpoints.
nodes.languageNotes: Composite primary key over the rollup dimensions turns the table into an upsert-based counter store rather than an event log.

nodes.name: maintenance_runs
nodes.summary: Execution log for scheduled maintenance operations (currently only data retention), recording the actor, start/completion timestamps and a JSON details payload per run.

nodes.name: 0007_email_notification_limits.sql
nodes.summary: Introduces the outbound email pipeline: creates feedback_email_queue with a claim-based work-queue design, backfills it from all existing feedback_submissions, and adds feedback_notification_days to cap notifications at three per day.
nodes.languageNotes: Combines DDL with a data-backfill INSERT ... SELECT in a single migration, and uses a partial index over unclaimed rows (WHERE claim_id IS NULL) as an efficient pending-work scan.

nodes.name: feedback_email_queue
nodes.summary: Durable outbound work queue holding a denormalized copy of each submission awaiting email notification, with claim_id/claimed_at fields implementing lease-based claiming so concurrent workers do not double-send.

nodes.name: feedback_notification_days
nodes.summary: Per-day counter enforcing the outbound notification budget, with a CHECK constraint hard-limiting sent_count to at most three emails per notification_day.

nodes.name: ARCHITECTURE_QA.md
nodes.summary: Pull-request review checklist covering the design questions clang-format and clang-tidy cannot check: source layering, ownership and lifetime, audio-thread boundary, coupling/testability, and when a change warrants a full OpenSpec design doc.

nodes.name: BUILDING.md
nodes.summary: Build guide covering CMake 3.25/C++20 prerequisites, the Linux helper script, the generic CMake workflow, compile_commands.json generation, the VERSION single source of truth, the six-target CI matrix, and CPack native installer generation.

nodes.summary: C++ readability conventions plus the hard real-time audio rules: code reachable from the JUCE audio callback must avoid heap allocation, locks, file/network I/O, logging, UI updates, and FFT work.

nodes.name: FEEDBACK.md
nodes.summary: Describes the in-app feedback client: the v1 wire contract, the configurable intake endpoint, the /v1/authorizations then /v1/submissions call sequence, Cloudflare Access protection of admin paths, D1 storage with three scheduled email runs per day, and the local-queue fallback when submission fails.

nodes.name: QA_STRATEGY.md
nodes.summary: Living CI/testing gap analysis from a July 2026 review, recording the quality baseline and planning six work areas (TypeScript service CI, cross-platform test execution, supply-chain hygiene, CodeQL scanning, governance docs, performance monitoring) with dependencies and suggested sequencing.

nodes.name: performance-audio-thread-safety.md
nodes.summary: Safety review record for RealTimeEventCapture, documenting that its record() path is bounded and noexcept, the single-producer/single-consumer lifecycle constraints, and the automated stress-test evidence backing those claims.
nodes.languageNotes: Relies on is_always_lock_free static assertions as compile-time proof that the callback path never falls back to a mutex on unsupported targets.

nodes.name: performance-hardware-acceptance.md
nodes.summary: Acceptance protocol gating the Performance Lab feature, specifying the reference hardware matrix, controlled measurement conditions, interleaved trial ordering, instrumentation calibration, correctness/equivalence criteria, and end-to-end sign-off tables tracking Linux as accepted with Windows and macOS pending.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses filled-in result tables as living evidence rather than a template, so the doc doubles as the audit trail for the PRACTICE_TAKES_ENABLE_PERFORMANCE_LAB gate.

nodes.name: .openspec.yaml
nodes.summary: OpenSpec change marker declaring the real-world-performance-benchmarking change as spec-driven and dated 2026-07-27. Tells the OpenSpec tooling which artifact set (proposal, design, tasks, specs) governs this change.

nodes.name: proposal.md
nodes.summary: Change proposal for a GUI-driven performance lab that runs repeatable end-to-end benchmark scenarios on physical hardware and compares optimization strategies against a baseline. nodes.name: design.md
