nodes.languageNotes: Marshals all UI state changes back to the message thread with juce::MessageManager::callAsync plus a SafePointer capture, so a destroyed component cannot be touched by a late completion callback.

nodes.name: FeedbackComponent.h
nodes.summary: Declares FeedbackComponent, the in-app feedback form component, along with its SubmissionState enum, private Draft data structure, and the full set of JUCE child controls it owns.
nodes.languageNotes: Multiple inheritance from juce::Component and private juce::Thread lets the component own its own submission worker without exposing threading in its public API.

nodes.name: FeedbackComponent
nodes.summary: Final JUCE component that presents the feedback form and privately inherits juce::Thread to submit drafts asynchronously; exposes only painting, layout, and setContextTag publicly.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRecordStore.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the on-disk persistence layer for benchmark run records, storing one immutable JSON file per run under a configurable directory and providing an atomic export helper. Enforces write-once semantics, run-id sanitisation against path traversal, and typed status codes for every failure mode.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses an anonymous namespace for file-local helpers and C++20 designated initialisers to build StoredRecordResult, keeping JUCE File/JSON I/O behind a small typed status enum instead of exceptions.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRecordStoreTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 test suite covering BenchmarkRecordStore save/list/load round-trips, corrupt and newer-schema error preservation, run-id path-traversal rejection, and atomic export of incomplete runs. Uses an RAII temporary-directory fixture so each case runs against an isolated filesystem location.
nodes.languageNotes: The RAII TemporaryDirectory struct calls REQUIRE inside its constructor, so setup failures abort the test case exactly like an in-body assertion.

nodes.name: isValidRunId
nodes.summary: Guards run identifiers against directory escape by rejecting empty strings, a leading '~', any of the separators '/', '\' or ':', and embedded '..' sequences.

nodes.name: writeFile
nodes.summary: Writes text to a JUCE file through an owned output stream with LF line endings, flushing and reporting whether the final stream status was OK.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRecordStore::save
nodes.summary: Persists a benchmark run record as JSON, validating the run id, creating the store directory on demand, and refusing to overwrite an existing record so saved runs stay immutable.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRecordStore::load
nodes.summary: Reads and decodes a stored run record by id, mapping each failure into a distinct status plus message: invalid id, not found, corrupt JSON, newer schema, or decode failure.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRecordStore::listRunIds
nodes.summary: Enumerates the store directory for top-level *.json files and returns their base names as a lexicographically sorted list of run identifiers.

nodes.name: exportBenchmarkRecord
nodes.summary: Exports a run record to an arbitrary destination path atomically by writing through a JUCE TemporaryFile and swapping it over the target only after the write succeeds.

nodes.name: jsonFor
nodes.summary: Encodes a benchmark run record through BenchmarkRecordCodec and renders it as pretty-printed JSON text, the single serialisation path shared by save and export.

nodes.name: TemporaryDirectory
nodes.summary: RAII test fixture that creates a unique directory under the system temp location on construction and deletes it recursively on destruction, isolating each store test case.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Cloudflare Worker entry point for the feedback intake service, exposing the public /v1/authorizations and /v1/submissions endpoints plus a scheduled handler for daily email batches and retention sweeps. Implements HMAC-signed authorization tokens, rate limiting, payload validation, and per-route request metrics.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>` so the default export is checked against the Workers runtime contract while keeping literal inference for fetch/scheduled.

nodes.name: admin.ts
nodes.summary: Cloudflare Access-gated administrative API and dashboard for triaging feedback submissions, covering listing, filtering, updating, deleting, CSV export, screenshot retrieval, and the audit trail. Also serves the bundled HTML/CSS/JS dashboard assets.
nodes.languageNotes: Imports .html/.css/.js assets as strings via Wrangler's text module rules, so dashboard assets ship inside the Worker bundle.

nodes.name: operations.ts
nodes.summary: Operational policy layer for the feedback service: storage capacity limits, data retention windows, request telemetry recording, database health checks, and the aggregated operational report used by the admin dashboard.

nodes.name: notifications.ts
nodes.summary: Batches pending feedback reports into daily digest emails sent through Cloudflare Email Service, using database-backed claims and per-day reservations to cap sends and survive concurrent scheduled invocations.
nodes.languageNotes: Claim/reservation rows act as a distributed lock so overlapping cron invocations cannot double-send the same batch.

nodes.name: docker-server.ts
nodes.summary: Standalone Node.js HTTP server that hosts the admin dashboard inside a Docker container, adapting the Cloudflare D1 REST API to the D1Database interface and guarding requests with HTTP Basic auth and same-origin checks.
nodes.languageNotes: RemoteStatement/RemoteD1 are shim classes that reimplement the Workers D1 binding surface on top of the Cloudflare REST API, letting admin.ts run unchanged outside Workers.

nodes.name: index.test.ts
nodes.summary: Node test-runner suite covering the public Worker endpoints: authorization issuance, token verification, feedback validation, rate limiting, and error codes, using an in-memory D1 double.

nodes.name: admin.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests for the admin API surface, verifying Access identity enforcement, submission listing and filtering, update/delete flows, and audit logging against a scripted D1 stub.

nodes.name: notifications.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests the daily feedback digest batching logic, asserting claim handling, per-day send caps, email content, and recovery from stale claims via a scripted database double.

nodes.name: handlePublicRequest
nodes.summary: Routes public HTTP requests to the health check, authorization, or submission handlers and returns method/path errors otherwise.

nodes.name: createAuthorization
nodes.summary: Validates an authorization request, applies per-client and global rate limits, and issues an HMAC-signed short-lived submission token.

nodes.name: createSubmission
nodes.summary: Handles a feedback submission end to end: token verification, payload and screenshot validation, storage capacity checks, quarantine screening, and idempotent insertion into D1.

nodes.name: readJson
nodes.summary: Reads and parses a JSON request body, enforcing the content type and a maximum body size before returning the decoded value.

nodes.name: validateAuthorizationRequest
nodes.summary: Checks that an authorization payload has the expected schema version, installation id, and a supported minimum app version, rejecting unknown fields.

nodes.name: validateFeedbackRequest
nodes.summary: Validates a feedback submission payload including category, message length, optional contact email, screenshot mime type, and client submission id.

nodes.name: isRateLimited
nodes.summary: Counts recent rows matching a client identifier within the sliding hour window to decide whether the caller exceeded its per-client quota.

nodes.name: isGlobalRateLimited
nodes.summary: Applies a service-wide hourly ceiling on a table to protect the backend from aggregate abuse independent of any single client.

nodes.name: verifyToken
nodes.summary: Decodes a base64url authorization token, recomputes its HMAC signature, and compares it in constant time before returning the claims.

nodes.name: compareVersions
nodes.summary: Compares two dotted numeric version strings segment by segment so the service can enforce a minimum supported app version.

nodes.name: handleAdminRequest
nodes.summary: Main admin router that requires an authenticated Access identity and dispatches to submission, audit, export, operations, retention, and static asset handlers.

nodes.name: listSubmissions
nodes.summary: Returns a filtered, paginated page of feedback submissions shaped for the admin dashboard.

nodes.name: getSubmission
nodes.summary: Fetches a single submission by receipt id and returns its presented form, or a 404 when it does not exist.

nodes.name: getSubmissionScreenshot
nodes.summary: Streams a submission's stored screenshot back with the recorded mime type and no-store caching headers.

nodes.name: createSubmission
nodes.summary: Lets an administrator manually create a feedback record from the dashboard, validating core fields and recording the action in the audit log.

nodes.name: filters
nodes.summary: Translates admin dashboard query parameters into a parameterised SQL WHERE clause with bound values.

nodes.name: updateSubmission
nodes.summary: Applies a partial update to a submission — status, priority, tags, notes, GitHub issue link, duplicate pointer — validating each field and writing an audit entry.

nodes.name: deleteSubmission
nodes.summary: Deletes a single submission by receipt id and records the deletion in the admin audit trail.

nodes.name: deleteSubmissions
nodes.summary: Performs a bulk delete of the receipt ids supplied in the request body, auditing each removal.

nodes.name: listAdminActions
nodes.summary: Returns a paginated view of the admin audit log for the audit dashboard page.

nodes.name: validateCoreFields
nodes.summary: Validates the shared submission fields (category, version, message, contact email) for admin-created records.

nodes.name: readObject
nodes.summary: Parses a JSON request body into a plain object, rejecting malformed or non-object payloads.

nodes.name: exportSubmissions
nodes.summary: Renders the filtered submission set as a downloadable CSV file with escaped cell values.

nodes.name: presentSubmission
nodes.summary: Maps a raw D1 submission row into the camel-cased dashboard representation, decoding tags and structured feedback fields.

nodes.name: parseStructuredFeedback
nodes.summary: Extracts structured sections (steps, expected, actual) out of a free-form feedback message body when the client submitted the templated format.

nodes.name: configuredPositiveInteger
nodes.summary: Parses an environment variable into a positive integer, falling back to a default when unset or invalid.

nodes.name: storageLimits
nodes.summary: Builds the storage limit set (max submissions, max bytes, per-installation cap) from environment configuration.

nodes.name: retentionPolicy
nodes.summary: Resolves the per-category data retention windows (resolved, duplicate, declined, telemetry, audit, email queue) from environment settings.

nodes.name: estimatedStoredBytes
nodes.summary: Estimates the storage footprint of an incoming submission including the decoded screenshot payload.

nodes.name: suspiciousSubmissionReason
nodes.summary: Screens a feedback message for spam or abuse markers and returns a quarantine reason when one matches.

nodes.name: checkStorageCapacity
nodes.summary: Verifies that accepting a new submission stays within the global row count, global byte, and per-installation limits, returning the violated bound when it does not.

nodes.name: recordRequestMetric
nodes.summary: Upserts a per-route, per-status telemetry bucket with request counts and duration totals for the operational report.

nodes.name: verifyDatabaseAvailability
nodes.summary: Runs a trivial query to confirm the D1 binding is reachable, backing the service health endpoint.

nodes.name: runRetention
nodes.summary: Executes the scheduled data retention sweep, purging aged submissions, authorization records, telemetry buckets, audit entries, and email queue rows, then records the maintenance run.

nodes.name: operationalReport
nodes.summary: Aggregates storage usage, submission status counts, request telemetry, and recent maintenance runs into the operations summary shown on the admin dashboard.

nodes.name: sendPendingFeedbackBatch
nodes.summary: Claims a batch of unnotified feedback reports, reserves a daily email slot, sends the digest through the email binding, and marks the reports as notified or releases the claim on failure.

nodes.name: feedbackEmailText
nodes.summary: Renders the plain-text body of the digest email, listing each report's metadata and message plus a dashboard link.

nodes.name: releaseClaim
nodes.summary: Clears the claim marker from feedback rows so a failed send can be retried by a later scheduled run.

nodes.name: releaseReservation
nodes.summary: Gives back a reserved daily email slot when the send fails, so the day's quota is not consumed by an unsent digest.

nodes.name: notificationConfiguration
nodes.summary: Resolves and validates the email sender, recipients, and dashboard URL from the environment, returning null when notifications are not fully configured.

nodes.name: isEmailAddress
nodes.summary: Performs a conservative structural check on an email address, enforcing length limits and a single well-formed local/domain split.

nodes.name: RemoteStatement
nodes.summary: Implements the D1PreparedStatement surface (bind/all/first/run) by forwarding SQL and bindings to the Cloudflare D1 REST API.

nodes.name: RemoteD1
nodes.summary: Minimal D1Database implementation that authenticates against the Cloudflare API and issues queries on behalf of the containerised admin dashboard.

nodes.name: authorized
nodes.summary: Validates an HTTP Basic Authorization header against the configured dashboard credentials using a constant-time comparison.

nodes.name: sameOriginRequest
nodes.summary: Rejects cross-site requests by comparing the incoming Origin header against the server's own host, mitigating CSRF against the dashboard.

nodes.name: MemoryStatement
nodes.summary: In-memory prepared-statement double that interprets the Worker's SQL well enough to exercise insert, count, and lookup paths in tests.

nodes.name: MemoryD1
nodes.summary: In-memory D1Database stand-in providing prepare, batch, and execute so the Worker can run without a real Cloudflare binding.

nodes.name: fetchWorker
nodes.summary: Invokes the Worker's default fetch handler with a synthetic execution context so tests can assert on real responses.

nodes.name: AdminStatement
nodes.summary: Scripted prepared-statement double that returns canned rows for the admin queries under test and records executed SQL.

nodes.name: AdminD1
nodes.summary: Lightweight D1Database double that hands out AdminStatement instances for the admin request tests.

nodes.name: NotificationStatement
nodes.summary: Prepared-statement double that simulates claim, reservation, and pending-report queries for the notification batching tests.

nodes.name: NotificationDatabase
nodes.summary: D1Database double that lets each test register scripted responses keyed by SQL fragment for the digest email flow.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Two-stage Docker build for the feedback-intake service: a build stage installs npm workspace dependencies and bundles the TypeScript sources with esbuild, and a slim runtime stage ships only the compiled bundle and entrypoint script, running as the unprivileged node user on port 8787.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a multi-stage build so npm toolchain and source files never reach the runtime image; the final stage drops to USER node and chowns /app, a standard hardening pattern for Node containers.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Build stage based on node:26-bookworm-slim that restores the npm workspace lockfile, copies the feedback-intake sources and tsconfig, and runs the build:docker esbuild bundle into /app/feedback-intake/dist.

nodes.name: runtime
nodes.summary: Runtime stage that copies only the bundled dist output and docker-entrypoint.sh from the build stage, fixes ownership, drops to the node user, and exposes port 8787 with the entrypoint script as the container command.

nodes.name: build-multiplatform.yml
nodes.summary: Reusable GitHub Actions workflow that compiles Practice Takes with CMake/Ninja across Linux, Windows, and macOS runners (x64 and arm64), packages each build with CPack into .deb/.exe/.pkg installers, code-signs and notarizes them, verifies the Linux package installs cleanly on Debian 12/13 and Ubuntu 22.04/24.04, then assembles a checksummed release-asset bundle. It is invoked directly on push and pull request and also exposed via workflow_call so the release pipeline can build a specific ref at a pinned version.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a matrix strategy plus a debian:12 job container so the dynamically linked binaries inherit the oldest supported glibc, which keeps the produced .deb installable on the compatibility baseline. Signing secrets are declared individually under workflow_call rather than inherited, and every signing step self-skips when its secret is absent.

nodes.name: release.yml
nodes.summary: Release orchestration workflow that calculates the next semantic version, commits the version bump and creates an immutable annotated tag, delegates artifact production to the reusable multiplatform build workflow, then verifies checksums, attests build provenance, and publishes the GitHub release with the six platform installers. Runs on manual dispatch with a patch/minor/major choice, or on push of a version tag.
nodes.languageNotes: A non-cancelling concurrency queue (queue: max) serializes releases so two runs cannot race the same tag. Provenance attestation and the SHA256SUMS re-check happen against the exact artifact set the publish step uploads, so the release notes can promise verifiability for every asset.

nodes.name: secret-scan.yml
nodes.summary: Security workflow with two independent jobs: gitleaks scans commit history for secret content, and a second job runs the repository's secrets manager in audit mode to reject tracked plaintext secrets. Triggered on push to main, on pull requests, and on a weekly cron that performs the full-history sweep the incremental scans cannot cover.
nodes.languageNotes: SARIF artifact upload and PR comments are explicitly disabled because those outputs quote matched secrets verbatim and would be publicly downloadable. Concurrency cancels only pull_request runs, since a push scans a unique commit range that must always complete.

nodes.name: services-check.yml
nodes.summary: Path-filtered quality gate for the services/ workspace that type-checks and tests the Node.js packages, and separately builds the feedback-intake container image to assert it still runs as a non-root user and that the bundled server file loads. Runs on pushes to main and pull requests that touch services/ or this workflow.
nodes.languageNotes: The container-build job exists because the image bundles the dashboard with esbuild resolved from the npm workspace, so a hoisting change from a dependency update can break the image while the type-check and test job still passes.

nodes.name: .pre-commit-config.yaml
nodes.summary: Pre-commit hook configuration wiring three local system hooks: SOPS secret encryption/staging, a plaintext-secret audit gate, and clang-format for C/C++ sources. Hooks are installed for both pre-commit and pre-merge-commit stages.
nodes.languageNotes: All hooks use `language: system` with `always_run: true` and `require_serial: true`, so the secrets scripts run once per commit regardless of which files changed.

nodes.name: .sops.yaml
nodes.summary: SOPS creation rules mapping every `.secrets/*.sops` file to a single age recipient key, so encrypted secrets in that directory are always sealed to the maintainer's key.

nodes.name: CMakeLists.txt
nodes.summary: Root CMake build configuration for Practice Takes: it validates and reads the VERSION file, stamps version/commit/build metadata into compile definitions, fetches pinned JUCE 8.0.12 and Catch2 v3.8.1, and declares the JUCE GUI app target plus the Catch2 test executable with its full source list.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses FetchContent with commit-pinned GIT_TAGs plus GIT_SHALLOW, applies Linux-only JUCE ALSA patches via helper modules, and gates the feedback endpoint's curl dependency behind a cache variable.

nodes.name: SECURITY.md
nodes.summary: Security policy describing private vulnerability reporting through GitHub security advisories and the supported-version rule: only the latest release is supported, with the v0.5.6 LTS branch documented as inactive groundwork.

nodes.name: vcpkg.json
nodes.summary: vcpkg manifest pinning the native dependency set for the Linux build — ALSA and JACK audio backends, curl with SSL only, fontconfig/freetype, and the X11 client libraries JUCE needs — against a fixed builtin baseline.
nodes.languageNotes: `builtin-baseline` pins the vcpkg registry commit so dependency versions are reproducible across machines and CI.

nodes.name: QUALITY.md
nodes.summary: Explains the project's code-quality pipeline across seven sections: local pre-commit clang-format and SOPS secret hooks, the post-merge clang-tidy auto-fix workflow on main, the check-only pull-request quality gate, manual clang-tidy usage, and VS Code IntelliSense setup against CMake's compilation database.
nodes.languageNotes: Documents a deliberate split between fast local formatting (clang-format in pre-commit) and slower repository-wide analysis (clang-tidy in CI), which keeps commit latency low while still enforcing analysis on main.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Index page for the contributor and maintainer documentation directory, linking to the building, architecture, QA, code style, quality, secrets, and releasing guides. Also lists the main technologies (C++20, JUCE 8, CMake, vcpkg, GitHub Actions) and the rule that the application version lives only in the root VERSION file.

nodes.name: RELEASING.md
nodes.summary: Maintainer guide to the release process: the root VERSION file as single source of truth, the manually dispatched GitHub Actions release workflow that tags an immutable source commit and publishes six verified platform packages, artifact provenance plus the not-yet-enabled Windows Authenticode and macOS Developer ID signing secrets, semantic-version selection, and local version.py commands.
nodes.languageNotes: Describes a tag-then-build release model: creating the version tag before building makes the release source immutable, so later pushes to main cannot invalidate a build already in progress.

nodes.name: SECRETS.md
nodes.summary: Operational guide to the SOPS/age secret-management scheme: plaintext secrets stay out of Git while encrypted mirrors live under .secrets/, driven by the secret-patterns globs and the sops-secrets and sops-secret-audit pre-commit hooks. Covers one-time key setup, recipient backup and rotation, the encrypt/decrypt/sync/resolve/audit commands of secrets_manager.py, and Git conflict resolution.
nodes.languageNotes: Explains the important distinction between `sops updatekeys` (re-wraps the existing data key, so removed recipients can still read old ciphertext) and `sops rotate` (generates a fresh data key) — plus why re-keying alone never revokes an exposed credential in public Git history.

nodes.name: .openspec.yaml
nodes.summary: Two-line OpenSpec change marker declaring the `spec-driven` schema and the 2026-07-31 creation date for the close-highest-risk-test-gaps change directory.

nodes.name: proposal.md
nodes.summary: Change proposal arguing that the feedback-intake worker's three hand-written D1 fakes never execute SQL and that the Python scripts' single test file is run by no workflow, then scoping the fix to a migration-seeded SQLite test adapter plus a Python CI gate. Declares the new `worker-database-fidelity` and `python-script-test-gate` capabilities and lists explicitly out-of-scope follow-ups.

nodes.name: design.md
nodes.summary: Technical design for the test-gap change, recording eight decisions — notably backing the test database with built-in `node:sqlite` rather than `better-sqlite3`, rejecting `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers`, applying the real migration files instead of a hand-written schema, and running Python tests via stdlib `unittest` discovery in a separate path-scoped workflow. Includes risks, a revert-only migration plan, and two open questions.
nodes.languageNotes: Follows the OpenSpec design template: Context, Goals/Non-Goals, numbered Decisions with rejected alternatives, Risks/Trade-offs tagged [Risk]/[Trade-off], Migration Plan, and Open Questions.

nodes.name: tasks.md
nodes.summary: Ordered implementation checklist of 24 tasks across six groups: the shared `test/support/database.ts` D1 adapter, the migration-integrity test, porting each database-backed Vitest suite one at a time, the new `python-check.yml` workflow, tests for `scripts/release/version.py`, and documentation/verification. Groups 1 and 2 are checked off; groups 3-6 remain open.

nodes.name: configure-cloudflare-access.sh
nodes.summary: Provisioning script that creates or updates the path-scoped Cloudflare Access application protecting the hosted feedback dashboard, then stores the resulting JWT audience, team domain, and notification email settings as encrypted Worker secrets via wrangler.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses strict Bash mode (set -euo pipefail) plus a hand-rolled .env parser that only sets variables not already exported, so caller-provided values win. API tokens are passed to curl through '--header @-' on stdin rather than argv, keeping the bearer token out of the process list.

nodes.name: usage
nodes.summary: Prints the here-doc help text describing the script's purpose and the required environment variables (account ID, setup API token, Access hostname, admin email, notification sender).

nodes.name: api_request
nodes.summary: Thin curl wrapper for the Cloudflare v4 REST API that takes a method, path, and optional JSON body, and injects the bearer token through stdin so it never appears in the process arguments.

nodes.name: require_success
nodes.summary: Validates a Cloudflare API response by checking the .success flag with jq, printing each returned error message and aborting when the named operation failed.

nodes.name: put_worker_secret
nodes.summary: Pipes a secret value into `wrangler secret put` from the feedback-intake service directory so Access and notification settings are stored as encrypted Worker secrets rather than plaintext config.

nodes.name: setup-dashboard-daemon.sh
nodes.summary: One-shot installer that bootstraps the self-hosted feedback dashboard as a systemd service: it generates the .env file, builds the Compose images, stages compose/env files under /etc/practice-takes-feedback, and writes and enables a root-owned systemd unit.
nodes.languageNotes: Because the generated unit runs as root, the script refuses any docker binary whose resolved path or ancestor directories are not root-owned and non-group/world-writable, and rejects unit field values containing characters outside a safe allowlist. Generated ExecStartPre lines assert the built images exist so the unit fails with an actionable message instead of silently rebuilding.

nodes.name: is_root_owned
nodes.summary: Returns success only when the given path is owned by uid 0 and has no group- or world-write permission bits, used as the primitive privilege-escalation check for the generated systemd unit.

nodes.name: trusted_binary_path
nodes.summary: Resolves a candidate executable through symlinks and echoes its real path only if the binary and every ancestor directory up to / are root-owned and not writable by unprivileged users.

nodes.name: require_unit_safe
nodes.summary: Aborts unit-file generation when a value destined for the systemd unit is empty or contains characters outside the safe allowlist, preventing injection into the ExecStart directives.

nodes.name: update-dashboard-daemon.sh
nodes.summary: Maintenance script that rebuilds the feedback dashboard Compose images with --pull, refreshes the staged compose and env files under /etc/practice-takes-feedback, and restarts the systemd service, optionally fast-forwarding the checkout first.
nodes.languageNotes: Warns when the installed unit file still references the in-checkout compose path, signalling that the older setup layout needs re-running of setup-dashboard-daemon.sh.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Complete operator and developer manual for the feedback-intake Cloudflare Worker, covering the public authorization/submission API, the Access-protected admin inbox, project layout, local development, the self-hosted Docker dashboard, deployment steps, the wire protocol, testing, security controls, retention/recovery operations, and credential rotation.
nodes.languageNotes: Runbook-style Markdown: every operational procedure is expressed as a copy-pasteable shell block, so the document doubles as the deployment script of record.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: npm manifest for the private @practice-takes/feedback-intake workspace, declaring ESM module type, Wrangler-based dev/deploy and D1 migration scripts, a vitest test task, and an esbuild bundle step that produces the self-hosted Docker dashboard server.
nodes.languageNotes: The build:docker script uses esbuild text loaders for .html/.css/.js so dashboard assets are inlined into a single Node bundle, mirroring how Wrangler's Text rules embed them in the Worker.

nodes.name: wrangler.example.jsonc
nodes.summary: Committed template for the git-ignored Wrangler config, defining the Worker entry point, Text-loader rules for dashboard assets, rate-limit and retention tuning vars, three daily cron triggers for the email queue, the send_email binding, and the D1 database binding with a placeholder database ID.
nodes.languageNotes: Secrets are deliberately absent: only non-sensitive tuning values live in vars, while signing keys and Access identifiers are supplied as encrypted Worker secrets, and the real wrangler.jsonc stays untracked.

nodes.name: dependabot.yml
nodes.summary: Dependabot configuration declaring three weekly update ecosystems: GitHub Actions at the repo root, npm rooted at the /services workspace (so the shared package-lock.json is updated in step with member manifests), and Docker base images for the feedback-intake service.
nodes.languageNotes: The npm entry deliberately points at /services rather than each package, because the npm workspace root owns the single lockfile.

nodes.name: python-script-test-gate/spec.md
nodes.summary: OpenSpec delta spec adding requirements for a CI gate that runs the repository's Python test suite on pull requests and pushes to main whenever files under scripts/ change, with automatic test discovery across the whole tree and explicit coverage of release version bump arithmetic.
nodes.languageNotes: Written in OpenSpec delta format: an 'ADDED Requirements' section where each SHALL-style requirement is paired with WHEN/THEN scenarios that serve as acceptance criteria.

nodes.name: worker-database-fidelity/spec.md
nodes.summary: OpenSpec delta spec requiring the feedback-intake worker's tests to run SQL against a real SQLite engine instead of a substring-matching fake, to build the test schema by applying the project's migration files in order, and to share one test database helper while exercising real database constraints.
nodes.languageNotes: OpenSpec delta format; the requirements are deliberately negative in places ('SHALL NOT define the schema by any other means') to forbid the fake-database pattern the change is replacing.

nodes.name: codeql-security-scanning/spec.md
nodes.summary: Baseline OpenSpec capability spec for CodeQL security scanning, requiring scans on pull requests to main, pushes to main, and a weekly schedule across the actions, c-cpp, javascript, python, and typescript languages. It now describes GitHub's CodeQL default setup rather than a repository workflow, since .github/workflows/codeql.yml was deleted and no file-based CodeQL workflow remains in the repo.
nodes.languageNotes: The spec explicitly states the scan is provided by GitHub-hosted default setup, so its requirements are verified through repository settings rather than by any file that can be read in this codebase.

nodes.name: build-and-run.sh
nodes.summary: Developer-facing Bash driver that configures, builds, and launches the Practice Takes JUCE application via CMake, pinning JUCE and Catch2 to exact commits and wiring optional vcpkg toolchain/triplet settings on Linux.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `set -euo pipefail` with array-built CMake argument lists, and shallow-clones JUCE/Catch2 itself so FetchContent never runs Git under a vcpkg-polluted environment.

nodes.name: secrets_manager.py
nodes.summary: Self-contained CLI that keeps plaintext secret files out of Git while mirroring them as SOPS-encrypted counterparts, offering audit, encrypt, decrypt, sync, resolve, and init subcommands plus staging guards.
nodes.languageNotes: Standard-library-only Python: argparse for the CLI, subprocess for git/sops shelling, and atomic temp-file-plus-rename writes so a crash never leaves a half-written secret.

nodes.name: test_secrets_manager.py
nodes.summary: Unittest suite covering the secrets manager's glob matching, path-traversal rejection, mirror round-tripping, conflict cleanup, and three-way plaintext merge behaviour.
nodes.languageNotes: Loads the sibling module through `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` instead of a package import, so the script directory needs no `__init__.py`.

nodes.name: secret-patterns
nodes.summary: Ordered, repository-relative glob rule list naming which plaintext files the SOPS secrets manager must mirror, with `!` exclusions keeping example and template files safely committable.
nodes.languageNotes: Rules are evaluated top to bottom and last-match-wins, so exclusion lines must follow the broader include they carve out of.

nodes.name: vitest.config.mts
nodes.summary: Vitest configuration for the services workspace that installs a pre-enforced inline plugin turning imported .html, .css, dashboard.js, and audit.js assets into default-exported text modules.
nodes.languageNotes: The `.mts` extension forces ESM parsing; the plugin uses the Rollup `\0` virtual-module prefix convention so the resolved asset ids never collide with real files.

nodes.name: SecretsError
nodes.summary: Domain exception raised for every recoverable secrets-management failure so the CLI can map it to a clean non-zero exit instead of a traceback.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Runs an external command with captured output, raising SecretsError with the child's stderr when the process fails.

nodes.name: read_patterns
nodes.summary: Parses the secret-patterns file into an ordered list of include/exclude rules, rejecting whitespace-bearing and traversing globs.

nodes.name: pattern_matches
nodes.summary: Tests a repository-relative path against a single glob rule, handling `**` prefixes so they match at the root as well as nested depths.

nodes.name: is_secret_path
nodes.summary: Applies the ordered rule list top to bottom, letting later exclusions override earlier includes, to decide whether a path is a managed secret.

nodes.name: discover_plaintext
nodes.summary: Walks the repository tree, skipping VCS and vendor directories, to collect every plaintext file the rules classify as a secret.

nodes.name: discover_mirrors
nodes.summary: Enumerates the encrypted mirror files that currently exist for the repository's managed secrets.

nodes.name: load_state
nodes.summary: Reads the JSON sync-state cache, returning an empty state when the file is absent or unparseable.

nodes.name: atomic_write
nodes.summary: Writes bytes to a temporary file and renames it into place, optionally applying owner-only permissions for secret material.

nodes.name: require_sops
nodes.summary: Locates the sops binary and verifies the repository carries the configuration needed to encrypt, failing loudly otherwise.

nodes.name: encrypt_bytes
nodes.summary: Encrypts plaintext bytes through sops for a specific mirror path, returning the ciphertext for atomic write.

nodes.name: decrypt_bytes
nodes.summary: Decrypts an encrypted mirror through sops and returns the recovered plaintext bytes.

nodes.name: sync_git_exclude
nodes.summary: Rewrites the managed block of .git/info/exclude so every plaintext secret pattern stays untracked without touching .gitignore.

nodes.name: staged_plaintext_paths
nodes.summary: Lists paths in the Git index that the pattern rules classify as plaintext secrets.

nodes.name: protect_staged_plaintext
nodes.summary: Guards commits by unstaging or refusing plaintext secrets that have found their way into the Git index.

nodes.name: audit_command
nodes.summary: Implements the `audit` subcommand, reporting discovered plaintext secrets, existing mirrors, and staging hazards.

nodes.name: encrypt_command
nodes.summary: Implements the `encrypt` subcommand, mirroring every discovered plaintext secret into a SOPS ciphertext and staging the result.

nodes.name: decrypt_command
nodes.summary: Implements the `decrypt` subcommand, restoring local plaintext files from their encrypted mirrors with an overwrite guard.

nodes.name: sync_command
nodes.summary: Implements the `sync` subcommand, reconciling plaintext and mirrors in both directions using recorded hashes and writing conflict copies when both sides diverged.

nodes.name: unmerged_mirrors
nodes.summary: Queries the Git index for mirror files left in an unmerged state after a conflicting merge.

nodes.name: decrypt_temporary_ciphertext
nodes.summary: Decrypts an in-memory ciphertext blob through a scratch file kept inside the .git directory so plaintext never lands in the worktree.

nodes.name: merge_plaintext
nodes.summary: Performs a three-way merge of decrypted secret versions, emitting standard conflict markers when the edits overlap.

nodes.name: resolve_command
nodes.summary: Implements the `resolve` subcommand, walking unmerged mirrors through decryption, three-way merge or side selection, and re-encryption.

nodes.name: init_command
nodes.summary: Implements the `init` subcommand, writing the .sops.yaml creation rule for the given age recipient and priming the Git exclude block.

nodes.name: build_parser
nodes.summary: Declares the argparse command-line surface, registering every subcommand and its options.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Process entry point that parses arguments, dispatches the selected subcommand, and translates SecretsError into a clean exit code.

nodes.name: temporary_repository
nodes.summary: Context manager fixture that yields a freshly initialised throwaway Git repository so Git-backed helpers can be exercised in isolation.

nodes.name: PatternTests
nodes.summary: Verifies glob semantics for the rule engine: `**` matching at root and nested depths, ordered exclusions winning, mirror path round-trips, and rejection of parent traversal or whitespace patterns.

nodes.name: RepositoryPatternTests
nodes.summary: Checks the repository's own secret-patterns file so managed plaintext is selected while example and template files stay excluded.

nodes.name: InitTests
nodes.summary: Asserts that `init` writes a .sops.yaml creation rule whose regex actually matches the mirror paths the manager produces.

nodes.name: SyncConflictTests
nodes.summary: Confirms that conflict copies written during sync are cleaned up once the conflict has been resolved.

nodes.name: PlaintextMergeTests
nodes.summary: Exercises three-way merging of secret files: non-overlapping edits merge cleanly, overlapping edits produce markers, and scratch plaintext never escapes the .git directory.

tour.title: Project Orientation
tour.description: Start here to learn what Practice Takes is: an early cross-platform desktop music-practice app built on JUCE, currently focused on live microphone analysis (a tuner and a spectrogram) inside a dockable/floating workspace, with the longer-term ambition of becoming a fuller DAW. The README covers the user-facing feature set and supported platforms, while ARCHITECTURE.md is the authoritative reference for the src/ layering, the MainComponent ownership model, and the real-time audio-thread boundary you will meet in later steps. CONTRIBUTING.md explains how work actually lands here — through the OpenSpec proposal workflow that closes this tour.

tour.title: Build System and Toolchain
tour.description: Before reading code, understand how it gets compiled. The root CMakeLists.txt is the highest fan-out node in the entire graph: it reads the VERSION file, stamps version/commit metadata into compile definitions, fetches pinned JUCE 8.0.12 and Catch2 v3.8.1, and declares both the GUI application target and the test executable with its full source list. vcpkg.json pins the native Linux dependency set (ALSA, JACK, curl, fontconfig, X11) against a fixed baseline, and build-and-run.sh is the one-command developer driver that configures, builds, and launches the app.
tour.languageLesson: CMake's FetchContent pins dependencies to exact commits or tags so every machine builds against identical sources, while vcpkg manifest mode declares system-level native libraries. Together they give a reproducible build without vendoring third-party code into the repository.

tour.title: Entry Point and Startup Sequence
tour.description: src/bootstrap/main.cpp is the process entry point: it defines PracticeTakesApplication and its MainWindow, handles per-platform fullscreen/kiosk behaviour, and owns a single MainComponent. Startup ordering is not incidental — WorkspaceStartupSequence.h encodes the contract as a header-only helper: restore the workspace first, then show the window, then defer service initialisation so the UI appears before the audio device is opened. MainComponent.h declares the application shell (the single most depended-upon C++ header, with roughly 80 member functions), and MainComponentLifecycle.cpp implements its construction, settings-file migration, top-bar wiring, and the microphone-permission warning overlay.
tour.languageLesson: C++ partial implementation across translation units: MainComponent is declared once in a header but its members are defined across a dozen .cpp files (lifecycle, workspace layout, drag, snapshot, settings, feedback). This keeps compile units small and topical without introducing inheritance or forwarding indirection.

tour.title: The Workspace State Model
tour.description: The dockable workspace rests on pure, JUCE-free data structures that can be unit tested without a UI. WorkspaceLayoutState.h models the tiling as a binary tree — leaves hold a single tool or a tab group, internal nodes are two-way splits, and a drop on a pane edge subdivides it indefinitely. WorkspaceToolState.h is a dependency-free state machine tracking closed/docked/floating and reporting whether a transition needs a fresh tool instance. WorkspaceBuiltIns.h defines the four shipped workspaces (Pitch Practice, Vocal Warm-up, Spectrum Analysis, Performance Preparation), and WorkspaceSnapshotCapture.h serialises the live tree plus floating bounds, tool settings, and focus into a persistable document.
tour.languageLesson: Separating a pure model from its rendering is the central testability trick in this codebase. These headers deliberately include no JUCE types, so the layout tree, the tool state machine, and snapshot serialisation can all be exercised in headless Catch2 tests.

tour.title: Docking, Dragging, and Floating
tour.description: This step is where the abstract tree from Step 4 becomes pixels. MainComponentWorkspaceLayout.cpp materialises WorkspaceLayoutState into live JUCE components, rebuilding split panes and tab groups on every layout change. DockedToolPanel.h wraps each docked tool in a titled container with a drag handle, options button, and the drag-threshold logic that tears a tool out into a floating window, while ToolWindow.h is the floating host on the other side of that transition. MainComponentWorkspaceDrag.cpp coordinates the drag gesture itself, translating pointer movement into the edge-drop subdivisions the model supports.

tour.title: Live Audio Capture and the FIFO
tour.description: Now follow the signal. AudioInputService.h declares the shared capture service, its InputState enum, the Listener interface every analysis tool implements, and the per-consumer FIFO slot layout — one slot per tool, so the tuner and spectrogram never contend for the same buffer. AudioSampleFifo.h is a header-only fixed-capacity single-producer/single-consumer ring buffer that hands samples from the device callback to a tool without locking or allocating. AudioRecoveryPolicy.h isolates the decision of when to reopen a failed device into a pure, side-effect-free policy precisely so it can be exhaustively unit tested.
tour.languageLesson: The real-time audio thread must never lock, allocate, or block. A single-producer/single-consumer ring buffer achieves that with plain atomic read/write indices, and dropping a whole block when full is preferred over stalling the callback — a dropped frame is recoverable, a missed deadline is an audible glitch.

tour.title: Pitch and Harmonic Analysis
tour.description: These two headers hold the DSP the app exists for. PitchDetector.h declares an allocation-free detector that owns fixed FFT and correlation scratch arrays up front, so a detection pass never touches the heap. HarmonicAnalyzer.h defines the harmonic-profile contract — fundamental, spectral centroid, confidence, inharmonicity, and relative partial amplitudes — consumed by both the harmonics UI in the next step and the Performance Lab benchmarks later. Both read from the FIFO slots introduced in Step 6 rather than from the device callback directly.
tour.languageLesson: Pre-sized member arrays instead of std::vector is a deliberate real-time C++ idiom: the object's memory footprint is fixed at construction, so the hot analysis path has no allocation, no reallocation, and fully predictable cache behaviour.

tour.title: The Tuner and Spectrogram Tools
tour.description: The user-visible half of the signal path. TunerComponent.cpp builds the tuner's control surface and settings model, then runs the loop that drains its FIFO slot, calls PitchDetector from Step 7, and confirms, smooths, and displays the detected note. SpectrogramComponent.cpp windows and FFTs live microphone blocks, shifts its image one column left per frame, and paints a logarithmic frequency grid on top. HarmonicAnalyzerComponent.cpp renders the harmonic profile. Each of these is a workspace tool, so any of them can be docked, tabbed, or torn off using the machinery from Step 5.

tour.title: In-App Feedback and the Shared Contract
tour.description: Practice Takes asks for feedback, but only at defensible moments. FeedbackInvitationPolicy.h is another pure policy header: it decides whether to offer an invitation based on successful tool uses, prior dismissal, an opt-out flag, and whether a session is live. MainComponentFeedback.cpp wires that policy into the Help menu and the feedback window using persisted application properties, and FeedbackComponent.h declares the form itself with its SubmissionState machine. The pivotal file is contracts/feedback/v1.schema.json — a JSON Schema defining the v1 wire protocol (client identity, authorization request, submission with optional screenshot, receipt) shared by the desktop client and the Worker in Step 10.
tour.languageLesson: A versioned JSON Schema checked into the repository acts as a language-neutral contract between a C++ client and a TypeScript server. Versioning it in the path (v1) means a future v2 can ship alongside it, letting older desktop installs keep submitting while new clients migrate.

tour.title: The Feedback Intake Worker
tour.description: services/feedback-intake is a Cloudflare Worker written in TypeScript that receives what Step 9 sends. index.ts is its entry point and router, exposing /v1/authorizations and /v1/submissions plus a scheduled handler, and implementing HMAC-signed authorization tokens, rate limiting, payload validation against the shared schema, and per-route metrics. access.ts verifies Cloudflare Access JWTs and fails closed on misconfiguration; admin.ts is the Access-gated triage API and dashboard; operations.ts centralises storage caps, retention windows, telemetry, and health checks; notifications.ts batches reports into daily digest emails using database-backed claims that survive concurrent cron invocations.
tour.languageLesson: A Cloudflare Worker exports a default object with `fetch` and `scheduled` handlers rather than starting a long-lived server. There is no persistent process memory between requests, which is why rate limits, email claims, and idempotency all have to live in the D1 database you will see next.

tour.title: Worker Storage and Container Packaging
tour.description: The Worker's durable state is a D1 (SQLite) database defined by ordered migration files. 0001_initial.sql creates feedback_submissions — receipt id, schema version, app version, hashed installation identity, category, message, optional contact — and every later migration extends it: 0006_operations.sql adds quarantine columns plus request_metrics and maintenance_runs, while 0007_email_notification_limits.sql introduces a claim-based feedback_email_queue and a per-day notification cap. The same code also runs outside Cloudflare: docker-server.ts is a plain Node HTTP server that adapts the D1 REST API to the D1Database interface for self-hosting, and the two-stage Dockerfile bundles it with esbuild and ships a slim runtime image running as an unprivileged user.
tour.languageLesson: SQL migrations are append-only and applied in filename order, so the schema's full history is reconstructible by replaying the directory — a property Step 14's in-flight change exploits to build test databases. On the Docker side, a two-stage build keeps npm and esbuild in the build stage so the runtime image carries only the bundled output.

tour.title: The Performance Lab
tour.description: A development-only benchmarking subsystem, compiled in only when PRACTICE_TAKES_ENABLE_PERFORMANCE_LAB is set. BenchmarkInterfaces.h has the highest fan-in of any file in the repository: it declares the abstract seams — BenchmarkClock, TelemetryCollector, BenchmarkScenario, OptimizationStrategy — that let every benchmark be driven by fakes in tests. BenchmarkTypes.h is the schema header defining the record version and every value type in a BenchmarkRunRecord, SustainedAudioAnalysisScenario.h exercises the Step 7 analysis path for a fixed frame count through a pure-virtual actions seam, and PerformanceLabController.cpp is the UI state machine handling validation, progress, cancellation, history, comparison, and export.
tour.languageLesson: Abstract base classes used purely as test seams (dependency inversion) explain why an interface header can be the most-imported file in a C++ project: production code depends on the contract, and both the real implementation and the test fake depend on it in turn.

tour.title: Tests, CI, and Quality Gates
tour.description: Every pure policy header you met earlier exists to be tested here. AudioSampleFifoTests.cpp covers wrap-around ordering, whole-block drops, per-consumer independence, and drop diagnostics; PitchDetectorTests.cpp validates the FFT detector against an independent scalar autocorrelation reference across sample rates; on the service side, index.test.ts exercises authorization issuance, validation, and rate limiting, with vitest.config.mts installing an inline plugin that turns imported HTML/CSS/JS dashboard assets into text modules. In CI, cpp-quality-check.yml enforces clang-format and clang-tidy on pull requests, services-check.yml type-checks and tests the Node workspace and verifies the container still runs as non-root, secret-scan.yml runs gitleaks plus the repository's own plaintext-secret audit, and build-multiplatform.yml compiles and packages installers across Linux, Windows, and macOS.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions path filters keep the pipeline fast: services-check.yml only runs when files under services/ change, while secret-scan.yml pairs incremental per-push scanning with a weekly cron that sweeps full history — the trade-off between fast feedback and thorough coverage made explicit in workflow configuration.

tour.title: OpenSpec and the In-Flight Change
tour.description: Changes to Practice Takes are proposed before they are written. openspec/specs/ holds canonical capability specs — workspace-layout-restoration/spec.md, for instance, defines how snapshots from Step 4 must restore safely across renamed tools, missing tools, and disconnected displays without blocking startup. openspec/changes/ holds active proposals: close-highest-risk-test-gaps argues that the Worker's hand-written D1 fakes never actually execute SQL and that the Python scripts' tests are run by no workflow, then scopes the fix to a migration-seeded SQLite adapter and a Python CI gate. Reading its proposal, design (eight recorded decisions, including choosing built-in node:sqlite over better-sqlite3), and 24-task checklist shows you exactly how this project reasons about a change before touching code.
tour.languageLesson: OpenSpec separates three artifacts: a proposal (why), a design (which trade-offs were weighed and rejected), and tasks (an ordered checklist), with delta specs describing how capability specs change. Recording rejected options is what makes the design document useful months later.
